## Async Jobs

### Get Task Status

> Retrieve the status and result of any async task using the poll_url returned by create endpoints

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/tasks/get-task-status

## Overview

Use this endpoint for unified async polling across task types such as video, image, music, and 3D generation.

If a create response includes `poll_url`, call that exact path. Some image models may return task-based responses under either an image-specific status path or `/v1/tasks/{id}`.

## Path Parameters

#### id

The task ID returned by the create request.

## Response

> Note: Fields describing results, errors, timestamps, and the model are returned when available for the task.

#### id

Canonical async task identifier.

#### task_id

Async task identifier alias.

#### poll_url

Preferred polling URL when the create response supplies one.

#### status

Task status such as `pending`, `processing`, `completed`, or `failed`. Cancelled tasks are represented as `failed` with `cancelled: true`.

#### cancelled

`true` when a queued async task was cancelled before execution.

#### cancellation_status

Cancellation marker. Present as `cancelled` when cancellation succeeds.

#### data

For completed image tasks, generated image results are returned here. Image tasks return URLs in `data[].url`.

#### progress

Optional progress value. Returned only when a real progress value is available; use `status` to determine completion.

#### video_url

Result asset URL when the task completes and produces a video.

#### video

Single video payload with `url`, `duration`, `width`, and `height` when available.

#### videos

Multiple video payloads when more than one output is available.

#### error

Error message when the task fails.

#### created

Creation timestamp when available.

#### updated

Last update timestamp when available.

#### model

Model used by the task when available.

## Error Behavior

An expired or unavailable public task can return `404 async_task_not_found`. If task ownership cannot be established for the current API key, the response is `403 task_not_owned`.

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Task not found or no longer available.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "async_task_not_found"
  }
}
```

## Examples

```bash cURL
curl "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/tasks/ldtask_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-api-key"
```

```python Python
import requests

poll_url = "/v1/tasks/ldtask_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"
response = requests.get(
    f"https://api.tokenlab.sh{poll_url}",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sk-your-api-key"},
)
print(response.json())
```

```javascript JavaScript
const pollUrl = '/v1/tasks/ldtask_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa';
const response = await fetch(`https://api.tokenlab.sh${pollUrl}`, {
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer sk-your-api-key' },
});
console.log(await response.json());
```

---

### Cancel Task

> Cancel a queued async task when the provider and model support cancellation

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/tasks/cancel-task

## Overview

Use `DELETE /v1/tasks/{id}` to cancel an asynchronous task that has not started running yet. Use the same task ID from the create response or the returned `poll_url`.

## Supported Tasks

Cancellation is available for queued Seedance tasks using `seedance-1.5-pro`, `seedance-2.0`, `seedance-2.0-fast`, or `seedance-2.5` when that task supports cancellation. A task already running or in a terminal state cannot be cancelled. Status remains queryable while its public task record is retained.

## Path Parameters

#### id

The async task ID returned by the create request or embedded in `poll_url`.

## Response

#### id

Canonical async task identifier.

#### task_id

Async task identifier alias.

#### poll_url

Preferred polling URL for the task. It remains valid after cancellation.

#### status

Task status. A successfully cancelled task is returned as `failed` with `cancelled: true` for compatibility with existing status values.

#### cancelled

`true` when the task was cancelled before execution.

#### cancellation_status

Cancellation marker. The value is `cancelled` when cancellation succeeds.

#### error

Cancellation reason or task failure message.

## Error Behavior

`400 unsupported_task_cancel` means the task type, provider, or model does not support cancellation. `409 task_not_cancellable` means the task is already processing, terminal, or otherwise no longer cancellable. `403` means the API key cannot access the task.

## Example

```bash cURL
curl -X DELETE "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/tasks/ldtask_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-api-key"
```

```json Response
{
  "id": "ldtask_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "task_id": "ldtask_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "poll_url": "/v1/tasks/ldtask_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "status": "failed",
  "cancelled": true,
  "cancellation_status": "cancelled",
  "error": "Task cancelled before execution"
}
```

## Gemini Native

### List Models

> List available models using Google Gemini API format

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/gemini/list-models

Returns a list of available models in Google Gemini API format.

## Query Parameters

#### pageSize

Maximum number of models to return. Default: `50`, maximum: `1000`.

#### pageToken

Continuation token returned by a previous page. Pass it back unchanged to fetch the next slice.

## Authentication

Authentication is not required for the public model catalog read endpoints.

Gemini-style auth hints such as `?key=` or `x-goog-api-key` do not change the response contract here.

## Response

#### models

Array of model objects.

#### nextPageToken

Returned when more models are available. Pass this value as `pageToken` to continue pagination.

## Errors

- Invalid `pageToken` returns `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- Unexpected list failures return `500 INTERNAL`.

```bash cURL
curl "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models?pageSize=5" \
  -H "x-goog-api-key: sk-your-api-key"
```

```python Python
import google.generativeai as genai

genai.configure(
    api_key="sk-your-api-key",
    transport="rest",
    client_options={"api_endpoint": "api.tokenlab.sh"}
)

for model in genai.list_models():
    print(model.name)
```

```javascript JavaScript
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models?pageSize=5",
  { headers: { "x-goog-api-key": "sk-your-api-key" } }
);
const { models } = await response.json();
models.forEach(m => console.log(m.name));
```

```json Response
{

    {

      "outputTokenLimit": 65536,
      "supportedGenerationMethods": [
        "generateContent",
        "countTokens"
      ],
      "baseModelId": "gemini-2.5-pro"
    },
    {
      "name": "models/gemini-3.5-flash",
      "version": "gemini-3.5-flash",
      "displayName": "gemini-3.5-flash",
      "description": "gemini-3.5-flash model available via TokenLab",
      "inputTokenLimit": 1048576,
      "outputTokenLimit": 65536,
      "supportedGenerationMethods": [
        "generateContent",
        "countTokens"
      ],
      "baseModelId": "gemini-3.5-flash"
    }

}
```

### Get Model

> Get model metadata using Google Gemini API format

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/gemini/get-model

Returns metadata for a specific model in Google Gemini API format.

## Path Parameters

#### model

Model name (e.g., `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-3.5-flash`). Aliases are also accepted.

## Authentication

Authentication is not required for the public model metadata read endpoint.

## Response

#### name

Model resource name in `models/{model}` format.

#### displayName

Human-readable model name.

#### inputTokenLimit

Maximum input tokens (context window).

#### outputTokenLimit

Maximum output tokens.

#### supportedGenerationMethods

List of supported generation methods (e.g., `generateContent`, `countTokens`, `embedContent`).

#### version

Public version string when available.

#### description

Human-readable model description when available.

#### temperature

Default temperature when the model provides one.

#### topP

Default top-p value when available.

#### topK

Default top-k value when available.

#### maxTemperature

Maximum supported temperature when available.

## Errors

- Invalid GETs that accidentally include `:generateContent` or `:streamGenerateContent` return `405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`.
- Missing models return `404 NOT_FOUND`.

```bash cURL
curl "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro"
```

```python Python
import google.generativeai as genai

genai.configure(
    api_key="sk-your-api-key",
    transport="rest",
    client_options={"api_endpoint": "api.tokenlab.sh"}
)

model = genai.get_model("models/gemini-2.5-pro")
print(f"Name: {model.name}")
print(f"Input limit: {model.input_token_limit}")
print(f"Output limit: {model.output_token_limit}")
```

```json Response
{
  "name": "models/gemini-2.5-pro",
  "version": "gemini-2.5-pro",
  "displayName": "gemini-2.5-pro",
  "description": "gemini-2.5-pro model available via TokenLab",
  "inputTokenLimit": 1048576,
  "outputTokenLimit": 65536,
  "supportedGenerationMethods": [
    "generateContent",
    "countTokens"
  ],
  "baseModelId": "gemini-2.5-pro"
}
```

### Generate Content

> Generates content using Google Gemini API format

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/gemini/generate-content

Use Gemini request and response formats with a model returned by the Gemini Models API. ProtoJSON lowerCamelCase and the corresponding proto snake_case field names are accepted. Supported optional fields and values depend on the selected model.

## Path Parameters

#### model

Model name (e.g., `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-3.5-flash`).

## Query Parameters

#### key

API key (alternative to header authentication).

## Authentication

Gemini endpoints support multiple authentication methods:
- `?key=YOUR_API_KEY` query parameter
- `x-goog-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY` header
- `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` header

## Request Body

#### contents

Conversation contents with `parts` and an optional `role`. Media parts use `inlineData` / `inline_data` or `fileData` / `file_data`. Files and Cache IDs created by TokenLab can only be used in their owning Workspace.

#### systemInstruction

System instruction for the model.

#### generationConfig

Generation settings such as `temperature`, `topP`, `topK`, `maxOutputTokens`, `stopSequences`, `candidateCount`, `responseModalities`, `responseMimeType`, `responseSchema`, and `thinkingConfig`. Corresponding snake_case names are also accepted. Supported values and combinations depend on the model.

#### safetySettings

Safety filter settings.

Every lowerCamelCase field shown above may also use its official proto `snake_case` spelling, for example `system_instruction`, `generation_config`, `safety_settings`, `tool_config`, `cached_content`, `file_data.file_uri`, and `inline_data.mime_type`.

## Supported Methods

The Gemini-compatible API includes model list/get, `generateContent`, `streamGenerateContent`, `countTokens`, `embedContent`, and `batchEmbedContents`. Gemini Interactions and Live are not available.

## Response

#### candidates

Generated content candidates.

#### usageMetadata

Token usage information.

```bash cURL
curl -X POST "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:generateContent?key=sk-your-api-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "contents": [
      {
        "parts": [{"text": "Hello, Gemini!"}]
      }
    ],
    "generationConfig": {
      "temperature": 0.7,
      "maxOutputTokens": 1024
    }
  }'
```

```python Python
import google.generativeai as genai

genai.configure(
    api_key="sk-your-api-key",
    transport="rest",
    client_options={"api_endpoint": "api.tokenlab.sh"}
)

model = genai.GenerativeModel("gemini-2.5-pro")
response = model.generate_content("Hello, Gemini!")

print(response.text)
```

```javascript JavaScript
import { GoogleGenerativeAI } from "@google/generative-ai";

const genAI = new GoogleGenerativeAI("sk-your-api-key");
const model = genAI.getGenerativeModel(
  { model: "gemini-2.5-pro" },
  { baseUrl: "https://api.tokenlab.sh" }
);
const result = await model.generateContent("Hello, Gemini!");

console.log(result.response.text());
```

```go Go
package main

import (
    "bytes"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "net/http"
)

func main() {
    payload := map[string]interface{}{
        "contents": []map[string]interface{}{
            {
                "parts": []map[string]string{
                    {"text": "Hello, Gemini!"},
                },
            },
        },
        "generationConfig": map[string]interface{}{
            "temperature":    0.7,
            "maxOutputTokens": 1024,
        },
    }

    jsonData, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
    req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST",
        "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:generateContent?key=sk-your-api-key",
        bytes.NewBuffer(jsonData))
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")

    client := &http.Client{}
    resp, _ := client.Do(req)
    defer resp.Body.Close()

    body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    fmt.Println(string(body))
}
```

```php PHP
<?php
$payload = [
    'contents' => [
        [
            'parts' => [
                ['text' => 'Hello, Gemini!']
            ]
        ]
    ],
    'generationConfig' => [
        'temperature' => 0.7,
        'maxOutputTokens' => 1024
    ]
];

$ch = curl_init('https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:generateContent?key=sk-your-api-key');

curl_setopt_array($ch, [
    CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
    CURLOPT_POST => true,
    CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => [
        'Content-Type: application/json'
    ],
    CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => json_encode($payload)
]);

$response = curl_exec($ch);
curl_close($ch);

$data = json_decode($response, true);
echo $data['candidates'][0]['content']['parts'][0]['text'];
```

## Vision Input Example

For Gemini multimodal requests, place media inside `contents[].parts[]` using either inline bytes or URL-based file references.

Supported media categories in the public Gemini contract:
- image
- audio
- video

For inline media, use either `inlineData` or `inline_data` and pass Base64-encoded file bytes.

For URL-based media, use either `fileData` or `file_data` and pass a public `https` URL.

## Video Input Example

```json
{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        { "text": "Please describe this video." },
        {
          "fileData": {
            "mimeType": "video/mp4",
            "fileUri": "https://example.com/demo.mp4"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Audio Input Example

```json
{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        { "text": "Please describe this audio." },
        {
          "fileData": {
            "mimeType": "audio/mpeg",
            "fileUri": "https://example.com/demo.mp3"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Image Input Example

Use inline image bytes:

```json
{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        { "text": "Please describe this image." },
        {
          "inlineData": {
            "mimeType": "image/jpeg",
            "data": "/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABAQ..."
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Use an image URL:

```json
{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        { "text": "Please describe this image." },
        {
          "fileData": {
            "mimeType": "image/jpeg",
            "fileUri": "https://example.com/demo.jpg"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Audio Input Example

Use an audio URL:

```json

      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        { "text": "Transcribe and summarize this audio." },
        {
          "file_data": {
```

## Video Input Example

Use a video URL:

```json

  "contents": [

      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        { "text": "Describe this video briefly." },
        {
```

### Stream Generate Content

> Streams content generation using Google Gemini API format

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/gemini/stream-generate-content

SSE version of Gemini `generateContent`. Events may contain only metadata or intermediate content without `finishReason`. The stream ends at natural EOF and does not append a `[DONE]` marker.

## Path Parameters

#### model

Model name (e.g., `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-3.5-flash`).

## Query Parameters

#### key

API key (alternative to header authentication).

## Request Body

Same as [Generate Content](/api-reference/gemini/generate-content). This includes multimodal `parts` arrays with structured `inline_data` image parts for vision requests.

Support for `generationConfig.candidateCount`, tools, media types, and other optional fields depends on the selected model.

## Response

Returns Gemini Server-Sent Events. Metadata-only events, intermediate chunks without `finishReason`, and natural EOF are valid. The stream does not append Chat Completions' `[DONE]` sentinel.

```bash cURL
curl -N -X POST "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:streamGenerateContent?key=sk-your-api-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "contents": [
      {
        "parts": [{"text": "Tell me a story"}]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

```python Python
import google.generativeai as genai

genai.configure(
    api_key="sk-your-api-key",
    transport="rest",
    client_options={"api_endpoint": "api.tokenlab.sh"}
)

model = genai.GenerativeModel("gemini-2.5-pro")
response = model.generate_content("Tell me a story", stream=True)

for chunk in response:
    for candidate in chunk.candidates:
        for part in candidate.content.parts:
            if part.text:
                print(part.text, end="")
```

```javascript JavaScript
const response = await fetch(
  'https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:streamGenerateContent?key=sk-your-api-key',
  {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      contents: [{ parts: [{ text: 'Tell me a story' }] }]
    })
  }
);

const reader = response.body.getReader();
const decoder = new TextDecoder();

while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  console.log(decoder.decode(value, { stream: true }));
}
```

```go Go
package main

import (
    "bufio"
    "bytes"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
)

func main() {
    payload := map[string]interface{}{
        "contents": []map[string]interface{}{
            {"parts": []map[string]string{{"text": "Tell me a story"}}},
        },
    }

    jsonData, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
    req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST",
        "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:streamGenerateContent?key=sk-your-api-key",
        bytes.NewBuffer(jsonData))
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")

    client := &http.Client{}
    resp, _ := client.Do(req)
    defer resp.Body.Close()

    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
    for scanner.Scan() {
        fmt.Println(scanner.Text())
    }
}
```

```php PHP
<?php
$payload = [
    'contents' => [
        ['parts' => [['text' => 'Tell me a story']]]
    ]
];

$ch = curl_init('https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:streamGenerateContent?key=sk-your-api-key');

curl_setopt_array($ch, [
    CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
    CURLOPT_POST => true,
    CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => ['Content-Type: application/json'],
    CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => json_encode($payload),
    CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION => function($ch, $data) {
        echo $data;
        return strlen($data);
    }
]);

curl_exec($ch);
curl_close($ch);
```

## Management

### Management API

> Check Workspace balances, manage API keys, and retrieve usage and billing

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/management/introduction

Use the Management API from your own backend or automation to manage a TokenLab Workspace. It uses a management token, so the program does not need a regular API key.

Create a management token in **Console → Settings**:

```bash
Authorization: Bearer mt-your-management-token
```

> Warning: Management tokens and API keys have different roles. Use `mt-...` only with `/v1/management/*`. Use `sk-...` with model APIs such as `/v1/responses`.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/management/balance` | GET | Get the Workspace balance |
| `/v1/management/api-keys` | GET | List API keys |
| `/v1/management/api-keys` | POST | Create an API key |
| `/v1/management/api-keys/{keyId}` | PATCH | Change its name, limit, models, expiration, or status |
| `/v1/management/api-keys/{keyId}/usage` | GET | Get individual usage records |
| `/v1/management/api-keys/{keyId}/billing` | GET | Get a billing summary |

## API Keys

- A new key's full secret appears only in the create response.
- `models: []` adds no key-level model restriction.
- `limitAmount: null` means unlimited. `0` prevents the key from incurring spend.
- Amounts use USD. Sending `CNY` returns `400 currency_retired`.
- `inactive` can be enabled again. Use `revoked` to retire a key permanently.

## Usage and Billing

`/usage` returns paginated records and supports model, model maker, scene, and date filters. Settled records can include `billing_transaction_id`; save it with `request_id` when you need to match a charge to a request.

`/billing` returns totals grouped by model, model maker, scene, and date. It does not include Workspace top-ups or invoices.

## Example

```bash
curl "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/management/balance" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mt-your-management-token"
```

## Next

- [Get Workspace Balance](/api-reference/management/get-balance)
- [List API Keys](/api-reference/management/list-api-keys)
- [Create an API Key](/api-reference/management/create-api-key)
- [Update an API Key](/api-reference/management/update-api-key)
- [Get API Key Usage](/api-reference/management/get-api-key-usage)
- [Get API Key Billing](/api-reference/management/get-api-key-billing)

### Get Workspace Balance

> Get the balance, top-ups, and usage spend for the current Workspace.

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/management/get-balance

## Overview

Return the balance, total top-ups, and total usage spend for the Workspace associated with the management token.

## Notes

- Monetary fields are USD-only.

- Amounts are returned in USD. Use `balance_decimal`, `total_recharge_decimal`, and `total_used_decimal` for exact calculations.

## Example

```bash cURL
curl -X GET "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/management/balance" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mt-your-management-token"
```

## Request / Response

This page provides the OpenAPI schema and copyable request examples. Send management requests from your terminal or client with a Management Token; direct sending is not available on this page.

## Response example

```json 200 OK
{
  "object": "organization_balance",
  "organization_id": "org_123",
  "balance": 42.5,
  "balance_decimal": "42.50",
  "total_recharge": 100,
  "total_recharge_decimal": "100",
  "total_used": 57.5,
  "total_used_decimal": "57.50"
}
```

## Important fields

#### object

Always `organization_balance`.

#### organization_id

Organization associated with the current management token.

#### balance

Current organization balance in USD as a JSON number for display.

#### balance_decimal

Exact current organization balance in USD as a decimal string for reconciliation.

#### total_recharge

Total successful organization recharge amount in USD as a JSON number for display.

#### total_recharge_decimal

Exact total successful organization recharge amount in USD as a decimal string for reconciliation.

#### total_used

Total organization usage spend in USD as a JSON number for display.

#### total_used_decimal

Exact total organization usage spend in USD as a decimal string for reconciliation.

### List API Keys

> Lists user-managed API keys for the current organization management token.

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/management/list-api-keys

## Overview

Returns user API keys in the organization associated with the current management token.

## Notes

- Monetary fields are USD-only.

- System-managed keys are excluded.

## Example

#### page

Page number starting at 1.

#### limit

Page size from 1 to 100.

```bash cURL
curl -X GET "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/management/api-keys" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mt-your-management-token"
```

## Request / Response

This page provides the OpenAPI schema and copyable request examples. Send management requests from your terminal or client with a Management Token; direct sending is not available on this page.

## Response example

```json 200 OK
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "key_abc123def456",
      "name": "Backend Worker",
      "key_prefix": "sk-live...",
      "status": "active",
      "limit_amount": 500,
      "limit_amount_decimal": "500",
      "used_amount": 148.25,
      "used_amount_decimal": "148.25",
      "models": [
        "gpt-5.6-luna",
        "claude-3-7-sonnet"
      ],
      "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
      "last_used_at": "2026-07-08T03:12:45.000Z",
      "created_at": "2026-07-01T10:00:00.000Z",
      "delivery_policy": null
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "limit": 50,
    "total": 1,
    "totalPages": 1
  }
}
```

## Important fields

#### object

Always `list`.

#### data

Array of API key objects.

#### pagination

Pagination metadata with `page`, `limit`, `total`, and `totalPages`.

#### data[].id

API key identifier used in follow-up Management API calls.

#### data[].name

Display name for the API key.

#### data[].key_prefix

Non-secret key prefix for display and support.

#### data[].status

One of `active`, `inactive`, `suspended`, or `revoked`.

#### data[].limit_amount

Spending cap in USD as a JSON number for display. `null` means unlimited.

#### data[].limit_amount_decimal

Exact spending cap in USD as a decimal string. `null` means unlimited.

#### data[].used_amount

Accumulated usage in USD as a JSON number for display.

#### data[].used_amount_decimal

Exact accumulated usage in USD as a decimal string.

#### data[].models

Per-key model allowlist. Empty array means no additional key-level model restriction.

#### data[].delivery_policy

`auto`, `verified`, `official`, `null`. `null` inherits the Workspace delivery policy.

#### data[].expires_at

ISO timestamp when the key expires, or `null` for no expiry.

#### data[].last_used_at

ISO timestamp for the most recent use, or `null` when unused.

#### data[].created_at

ISO creation timestamp.

### Create API Key

> Create an API key for the current Workspace.

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/management/create-api-key

## Overview

Create an API key in the Workspace associated with the management token. The full secret appears once, in this response.

## Request Body

| Field | Type | Default / Limits | Notes |
|-------|------|------------------|-------|
| `name` | string | optional, default `Default Key`, length `1-50` | Display name, trimmed server-side |
| `limitAmount` | number \| string \| null | `0–100000` USD | `null` means unlimited; `0` prevents spend. Decimal strings support up to 6 decimal places. Omitting this field when creating a key means unlimited. |
| `limitCurrency` | enum | default `USD` | USD only. Sending `CNY` returns `400 currency_retired`. |
| `models` | string[] | default `[]` | Optional model allowlist |
| `deliveryPolicy` | string \| null | `auto`, `verified`, `official`, `null` | `null` inherits the Workspace delivery policy. |
| `expiresAt` | string \| null | RFC3339 datetime | `null` means no expiry |

## Notes

- Monetary fields are USD-only. `CNY` inputs are retired and return `400 currency_retired`.

- `models: []` adds no key-level model restriction.
- `limitAmount: 0` creates a key that is valid but cannot spend quota until updated.

## Example

```bash cURL
curl -X POST "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/management/api-keys" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mt-your-management-token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Backend Worker",
    "limitAmount": 500,
    "models": ["veo3.1", "kling-3.0-video"],
    "expiresAt": "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z"
  }'
```

## Request / Response

This page provides the OpenAPI schema and copyable request examples. Send management requests from your terminal or client with a Management Token; direct sending is not available on this page.

## Response example

```json 201 Created
{
  "id": "key_abc123def456",
  "name": "Backend Worker",
  "key": "sk-live-redacted",
  "key_prefix": "sk-live...",
  "status": "active",
  "limit_amount": 500,
  "limit_amount_decimal": "500",
  "used_amount": 0,
  "used_amount_decimal": "0",
  "models": [
    "veo3.1",
    "kling-3.0-video"
  ],
  "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
  "last_used_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-07-08T03:00:00.000Z",
  "delivery_policy": null
}
```

## Important fields

#### key

Full secret API key value. It is returned only once on creation.

#### id

API key identifier used in follow-up Management API calls.

#### name

Display name for the API key.

#### key_prefix

Non-secret key prefix for display and support.

#### status

One of `active`, `inactive`, `suspended`, or `revoked`.

#### limit_amount

Spending cap in USD as a JSON number for display. `null` means unlimited.

#### limit_amount_decimal

Exact spending cap in USD as a decimal string. `null` means unlimited.

#### used_amount

Accumulated usage in USD as a JSON number for display.

#### used_amount_decimal

Exact accumulated usage in USD as a decimal string.

#### models

Per-key model allowlist. Empty array means no additional key-level model restriction.

#### delivery_policy

`auto`, `verified`, `official`, `null`. `null` inherits the Workspace delivery policy.

#### expires_at

ISO timestamp when the key expires, or `null` for no expiry.

#### last_used_at

ISO timestamp for the most recent use, or `null` when unused.

#### created_at

ISO creation timestamp.

### Update API Key

> Update an API key in the current Workspace.

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/management/update-api-key

## Overview

Use this endpoint to update the name, usage limit, allowed models, expiry, or status of an existing user API key.

## Request Body

At least one field must be provided.

| Field | Type | Default / Limits | Notes |
|-------|------|------------------|-------|
| `status` | enum | - | `active`, `inactive`, `revoked` |
| `name` | string | length `1-50` | Updated display name |
| `limitAmount` | number \| string \| null | `0–100000` USD | `null` means unlimited; `0` prevents spend. Decimal strings support up to 6 decimal places. |
| `limitCurrency` | enum | default `USD` | USD only. Sending `CNY` returns `400 currency_retired`. When set, `limitAmount` is required. |
| `models` | string[] | - | Updated model allowlist |
| `deliveryPolicy` | string \| null | `auto`, `verified`, `official`, `null` | `null` inherits the Workspace delivery policy. |
| `expiresAt` | string \| null | RFC3339 datetime | `null` clears the expiry |

## Notes

- Monetary fields are USD-only. `CNY` inputs are retired and return `400 currency_retired`.

- The Management API does not provide deletion. Use `inactive` for a temporary pause and `revoked` to retire a key permanently.
- Replace a revoked key with a new one.

## Example

```bash cURL
curl -X PATCH "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/management/api-keys/key_abc123def456" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mt-your-management-token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "status": "inactive",
    "limitAmount": 0
  }'
```

## Request / Response

This page provides the OpenAPI schema and copyable request examples. Send management requests from your terminal or client with a Management Token; direct sending is not available on this page.

## Response example

```json 200 OK
{
  "id": "key_abc123def456",
  "name": "Backend Worker",
  "key_prefix": "sk-live...",
  "status": "inactive",
  "limit_amount": 0,
  "limit_amount_decimal": "0",
  "used_amount": 148.25,
  "used_amount_decimal": "148.25",
  "models": [
    "gpt-5.6-luna",
    "claude-3-7-sonnet"
  ],
  "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
  "last_used_at": "2026-07-08T03:12:45.000Z",
  "created_at": "2026-07-01T10:00:00.000Z",
  "delivery_policy": null
}
```

## Important fields

#### id

API key identifier used in follow-up Management API calls.

#### name

Display name for the API key.

#### key_prefix

Non-secret key prefix for display and support.

#### status

One of `active`, `inactive`, `suspended`, or `revoked`.

#### limit_amount

Spending cap in USD as a JSON number for display. `null` means unlimited.

#### limit_amount_decimal

Exact spending cap in USD as a decimal string. `null` means unlimited.

#### used_amount

Accumulated usage in USD as a JSON number for display.

#### used_amount_decimal

Exact accumulated usage in USD as a decimal string.

#### models

Per-key model allowlist. Empty array means no additional key-level model restriction.

#### delivery_policy

`auto`, `verified`, `official`, `null`. `null` inherits the Workspace delivery policy.

#### expires_at

ISO timestamp when the key expires, or `null` for no expiry.

#### last_used_at

ISO timestamp for the most recent use, or `null` when unused.

#### created_at

ISO creation timestamp.

### Get API Key Usage

> Returns paginated usage details for a user API key.

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/management/get-api-key-usage

## Overview

Return paginated usage records for one API key.

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default / Limits | Notes |
|-----------|------|------------------|-------|
| `page` | integer | default `1`, min `1` | 1-based page number |
| `limit` | integer | default `50`, min `1`, max `100` | Page size |
| `model` | string | max length `100` | Requested model name |
| `modelVendor` | string | max length `100` | Public model vendor |
| `scene` | enum | - | `chat`, `image`, `audio`, `video`, `embedding`, `rerank`, `translation`, `music`, `3d`, `realtime` |
| `startDate` | string | - | Inclusive lower bound; accepts RFC3339 with timezone or `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `endDate` | string | - | Inclusive upper bound; accepts RFC3339 with timezone or `YYYY-MM-DD` |

If both `startDate` and `endDate` are present, `startDate` must be earlier than or equal to `endDate`.

## Notes

- Monetary fields are USD-only.

- The response is paginated.
- Settled records can include `billing_transaction_id`. Save it with `request_id` when you need to match a charge to a request.

## Example

```bash cURL
curl "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/management/api-keys/key_abc123def456/usage?page=1&limit=20&scene=chat&startDate=2026-07-01&endDate=2026-07-31" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mt-your-management-token"
```

## Request / Response

This page provides the OpenAPI schema and copyable request examples. Send management requests from your terminal or client with a Management Token; direct sending is not available on this page.

## Response example

```json 200 OK

  "api_key": {
```

### Get API Key Billing

> Returns aggregated billing breakdowns for a user API key.

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/api-reference/management/get-api-key-billing

## Overview

Return total spend, request count, billable usage, and cost grouped by model, model maker, scene, and date.

## Notes

- Monetary fields are USD-only.

- Workspace top-ups and invoices are not included.

## Example

Supports the same model, model vendor, scene, and date filters as [API key usage](/api-reference/management/get-api-key-usage). Returns totals without pagination.

```bash cURL
curl -X GET "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/management/api-keys/key_abc123def456/billing?startDate=2026-07-01&endDate=2026-07-31" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mt-your-management-token"
```

# Integrations


## Compatibility Matrix

### Tool and SDK compatibility

> Find the right TokenLab setup for coding tools, chat apps, SDKs, and frameworks

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/guides/ide-sdk-compatibility

Most tools connect to TokenLab by changing an API key and base URL. The exact setup depends on which API format the tool can use.

| API format | Base URL | Common clients |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions (OpenAI-compatible) | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` | OpenAI SDKs, many chat apps and frameworks |
| OpenAI Responses | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` | Responses clients and tools built around Responses events |
| Anthropic Messages | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` | Anthropic SDKs and Claude-oriented tools |
| Gemini | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` | Gemini REST and SDK clients that allow a custom host |

The selected model must list the same format in `accepted_request_formats`. Streaming and tool calling also depend on the model’s capabilities and the client. See [API formats](/guides/api-formats) for examples.

## Compatibility labels

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Works** | The linked TokenLab setup uses the client’s documented configuration options |
| **Works with limits** | The configuration applies to specific features or authentication modes; other vendor services keep their own requirements |

These labels describe the configuration on the linked page. Feature availability also depends on the selected model and client version.

## Coding tools

| Tool | Status | API format | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Claude Code](/integrations/claude-code) | Works | Anthropic Messages | Uses `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and a TokenLab API key |
| [Codex CLI](/integrations/codex-cli) | Works with limits | Responses | Uses Responses; available features depend on the selected model |
| [Cursor](/integrations/cursor) | Works with limits | OpenAI-compatible | Applies to Cursor features that accept a custom API key and URL |
| [Cline](/integrations/cline) | Works | OpenAI-compatible | Select **OpenAI Compatible** and enter a base URL and model ID |
| [Kilo Code](/integrations/kilo-code) | Works | OpenAI-compatible | Uses a custom provider and model ID |
| [OpenCode](/integrations/opencode) | Works | OpenAI-compatible | Load a separate provider configuration with `OPENCODE_CONFIG` |
| [OpenHands](/integrations/openhands) | Works | OpenAI-compatible | LiteLLM-backed UI: **Advanced → Custom Model** (`openai/` prefix) and **Base URL** |
| [Gemini CLI](/integrations/gemini-cli) | Works with limits | Gemini | Use `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` with API-key authentication; a separate `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` preserves the existing setup |

| [Chatbox](/integrations/chatbox) | Works | Add an **OpenAI API Compatible** provider |
| [Cherry Studio](/integrations/cherry-studio) | Works | Add a provider and complete **Verify and Enable** |

| [Open WebUI](/integrations/open-webui) | Works | Add an OpenAI-compatible connection with API Type **Chat** |

## SDKs and frameworks

| Client | Status | Setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [OpenAI SDK](/integrations/openai-sdk) | Works | Set `base_url` / `baseURL` to `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| [Anthropic SDK](/integrations/anthropic-sdk) | Works | Set the base URL to `https://api.tokenlab.sh` |
| [Vercel AI SDK](/integrations/vercel-ai-sdk) | Works | Create a custom OpenAI-compatible provider |
| [LangChain](/integrations/langchain) | Works | Configure `ChatOpenAI` or `OpenAIEmbeddings` with the TokenLab URL |
| [LlamaIndex](/integrations/llamaindex) | Works | Use its OpenAI-compatible client options |
| [OpenAI Agents SDK](/integrations/openai-agents-sdk) | Works with limits | The guide uses `OpenAIChatCompletionsModel`; check model and SDK feature support before using Responses |
| [AutoGen](/integrations/autogen) | Works | Use an OpenAI-compatible model client |
| [CrewAI](/integrations/crewai) | Works | Configure its OpenAI-compatible LLM client |
| [PydanticAI](/integrations/pydantic-ai) | Works | Supply an OpenAI-compatible provider |

More frameworks, observability tools, gateways, and evaluation products are listed in the Integrations navigation.

## Usage in streamed responses

Chat Completions streams accept `stream_options: { include_usage: true }`, which appends a final usage chunk before the stream closes. The Responses API does not expose `include_usage`; Responses streams report usage on their terminal event instead.

## What a custom API key does not replace

Some products mix model calls with features hosted by the product vendor. A TokenLab key can power the model requests exposed through BYOK settings, but it does not replace unrelated subscriptions, autocomplete services, account features, or proprietary extensions.

When a tool update changes its configuration, use the current integration page rather than copying an old environment-variable snippet from elsewhere.

## Before depending on a feature

- Confirm the tool allows a custom base URL for the format you need.
- Confirm the model lists that format in `accepted_request_formats`.
- Test streaming and tool calls if your workflow requires them.
- Keep the API key on a trusted machine or server.
- Record the Request ID when reporting a failure.

---

### SDKs & Libraries

> Use TokenLab with the SDK already in your application

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/guides/sdks

## Overview

You do not need a TokenLab-specific SDK. Keep the client your application already uses and change its API key and base URL:

- **OpenAI SDKs** work with Chat Completions and Responses.
- **Anthropic SDKs** work with Claude Messages.
- **Gemini / Google AI SDKs** work with Gemini requests.

Open the matching integration page for client configuration and model-specific limits. For a complete first request, use the [Quickstart](/quickstart).
## Choose an SDK

#### [OpenAI Python](https://github.com/openai/openai-python)

`pip install openai`

#### [OpenAI Node](https://github.com/openai/openai-node)

`npm install openai`

#### [OpenAI Go](https://github.com/openai/openai-go)

`go get github.com/openai/openai-go/v3`

#### [Anthropic SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)

Native Claude Messages API support

## OpenAI SDK Example

Use this for Chat Completions or Responses. The selected model must support the API method you call.

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="sk-your-api-key",
    base_url="https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1"
)

response = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5.6-terra",
    input="Reply with: Connected to TokenLab."
)

print(response.output_text)
```

## OpenAI Go Example

```go
package main

import (
    openai "github.com/openai/openai-go/v3"
    "github.com/openai/openai-go/v3/option"
)

func main() {
    client := openai.NewClient(
        option.WithAPIKey("sk-your-api-key"),
        option.WithBaseURL("https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1"),
    )

    _ = client
}
```

## Anthropic SDK Example

```python
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    api_key="sk-your-api-key",
    base_url="https://api.tokenlab.sh"
)

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

## Which SDK should you use?

| Need | SDK |
|------|------------------|
| Existing OpenAI-compatible client | OpenAI SDK on TokenLab `/v1` |
| Chat Completions, Responses, or embeddings | OpenAI SDK |
| Claude Messages fields | Anthropic SDK |
| Gemini contents, files, cache, or tools | Gemini / Google AI SDK |
| LangChain / LlamaIndex / Vercel AI SDK | Use the dedicated integration pages |

## Configuration notes

#### Keep model-specific fields in their API format

Claude Messages and Gemini represent tools, streaming, and content differently. Use the matching SDK when your application depends on those fields.

#### Keep existing OpenAI clients

Existing OpenAI-compatible chat and embedding clients can usually connect by changing the API key and base URL.

#### Keep base URLs explicit

Pass TokenLab base URLs directly in your client configuration instead of relying on older environment-variable aliases.

---


## Coding Tools

### Control coding agent costs

> Use real usage data to spend less without weakening every task

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/guides/coding-agent-cost

Coding agents repeatedly send instructions, conversation history, code, and tool results. Long sessions can therefore cost much more than a single chat request. The useful levers are model choice, context size, output length, and caching when the selected model supports it.

## Start with your own usage

Open [Usage](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/usage) in the workspace that owns your API key and compare requests by model or key. Compare similar tasks rather than relying on a generic hourly estimate.

Record at least:

- input, output, and cached tokens
- cost per completed task
- failed or repeated requests
- the model and API key used

## Match the model to the work

The most expensive model does not need to handle every step.

| Work | What to optimize |
|---|---|
| Architecture or difficult debugging | Reasoning quality and enough context |
| Focused edits and routine review | Reliable instruction following at a lower price |
| Search, classification, and boilerplate | Speed and low input cost |
| Final review | Quality on a smaller, carefully selected context |

Use the [Models page](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models) for current prices and capabilities. Test candidate models on the same representative task before changing a production tool.

## Keep context intentional

- Include the files and logs needed for the current task, not the whole repository by default.
- Start a new conversation when old history no longer helps.
- Let the agent search for code instead of pasting large directories into every prompt.
- Keep reusable instructions short and remove duplicated rules.

## Limit unnecessary output

Set the output limit supported by your selected [API format](/guides/api-formats) when the task has a predictable answer length. Chat Completions and Messages use different request shapes from Responses; use the endpoint’s documented field.

A limit prevents accidental long responses, but it should still leave enough room for the task to finish.

## Use caching only when it is documented

Some models charge less for cached input. Check the model's price details before counting on a cache discount, and confirm cached-token usage in the response or Usage. Cache behavior and prices differ by model.

## Separate projects with API keys

Use a different API key for each project or coding tool when you need separate limits and usage history. A key-level limit can stop one tool from consuming the full account balance.

## Compare changes with real tasks

1. Choose a small set of tasks that represents your normal work.
2. Run the same tasks with each candidate model and the same context.
3. Compare completion quality, retries, total tokens, and final cost in Usage.

The lowest price per token is not always the lowest cost per completed task. A cheaper request that needs several retries may cost more.

## Tool setup

#### [Claude Code](/integrations/claude-code)

Connect Claude Code with the Anthropic-compatible API.

#### [Codex CLI](/integrations/codex-cli)

Configure the TokenLab base URL and API key.

#### [Cursor](/integrations/cursor)

Review the supported BYOK boundary before setup.

#### [OpenCode](/integrations/opencode)

Add TokenLab as a custom provider.

---

### Choose a model for coding agents

> Compare coding models with the work, context, speed, and budget that matter to you

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/guides/coding-agent-models

There is no single best coding model. A model that is excellent at a small patch may be a poor fit for a repository-wide change, and leaderboard results do not predict how well it will follow your own instructions and tools.

Use the [Models page](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models) for current model IDs, context limits, API formats, and TokenLab prices. Do not copy a permanent recommendation list into your configuration.

## Match the model to the job

| Work | What matters most |
| --- | --- |
| Small edits and autocomplete | Fast responses, low cost, reliable instruction following |
| Debugging | Reading logs and code together, testing hypotheses, staying within scope |
| Code review | Finding concrete defects without flooding the review with speculation |
| Large refactors | Enough context, consistent changes across files, and strong tool use |
| Architecture | Clear tradeoffs, evidence from the repository, and good long-form reasoning |

Use a smaller context for focused work even when the model supports a very large window. More context costs more and can bury the relevant code.

## Compare candidates on your own tasks

Choose a few real tasks that represent the work you do. Give each candidate the same repository state, instructions, tools, and time limit. Compare:

- whether the change is correct and complete
- tests passed and regressions introduced
- unnecessary files or code changed
- total tokens and final TokenLab cost
- time to a usable result
- how often a person had to correct the agent

Keep results by task type. One model can be your best reviewer while another is better for implementation or quick edits.

## Keep model changes visible

Set the model explicitly in the coding tool. If your application offers a fallback, tell the user when the model changes. A fallback may have a different price, context limit, tool format, or output style.

The API format also matters:

| Tool or model need | Format | Base URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI-compatible chat | Chat Completions | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| Responses events or tools | Responses | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| Claude Messages features | Anthropic Messages | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` |
| Gemini content and tools | Gemini | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` |

Check `accepted_request_formats` for the selected model instead of inferring the format from its name.

## Coding tool guides

#### [Claude Code](/integrations/claude-code)

Use the Anthropic Messages API and a TokenLab API key.

#### [Codex CLI](/integrations/codex-cli)

Configure the TokenLab base URL and review Responses support.

#### [Cursor](/integrations/cursor)

Use Cursor's custom OpenAI-compatible settings where BYOK is supported.

#### [OpenCode](/integrations/opencode)

Add TokenLab as a custom model provider.

For cost controls, separate API keys, and usage comparison, continue with [Control coding agent costs](/guides/coding-agent-cost).

### TokenLab Provider Setup

> Connect a self-hosted OpenClaw instance to TokenLab

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/guides/tokenlab-provider

## Let my agent set this up

Copy this task to an agent already running on your computer:

```text
Read this guide and help me connect OpenClaw to TokenLab:
https://docs.tokenlab.sh/guides/tokenlab-provider
Check my installed version and active configuration first.
Preserve existing accounts, providers, permissions and other settings.
Back up local files and show proposed changes.
Have me enter any API key locally; never ask for, print or paste it in chat.
Check configuration loading first.
Explain any paid request test separately before running it.
```

> Note: This guide is for **self-hosted OpenClaw**. The TokenLab plugin is the shortest setup; manual configuration is available when you need a specific API format.

## Install the plugin

Optional: install the published provider plugin **0.1.0**. Supply `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` through the same Gateway environment described below and use session-only model selection. The plugin onboarding wizard changes the default model, so this guide does not run `openclaw onboard`. Keep existing plugin entries and permissions. Check the installed plugin and model list before making a request.

Review the capabilities requested by the installer and follow the client’s confirmation prompts. Do not grant unrelated permissions or change the permissions of existing plugins.

```bash
openclaw plugins install @tokenlabai/openclaw-provider@0.1.0
openclaw plugins list
openclaw models list --provider tokenlab
```

```text
/model tokenlab/claude-sonnet-5 -s
/model default -s
```

[npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tokenlabai/openclaw-provider/v/0.1.0) · [GitHub](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-openclaw-provider)

## Configure providers manually

Use `models.providers` only when OpenClaw needs Responses, Claude Messages, Gemini, or MiniMax formats separately. For ordinary chat, the `tokenlab` entry is enough.

| Provider | OpenClaw `api` | Best for | baseUrl |
|----------|----------------|----------|---------|
| `tokenlab` | `openai-completions` | GPT, DeepSeek, Qwen, and most OpenAI-compatible calls | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| `tokenlab-responses` | `openai-responses` | OpenAI Responses workflows that expect `/v1/responses` semantics | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| `tokenlab-claude` | `anthropic-messages` | Native Claude Messages API | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` |
| `tokenlab-gemini` | `google-generative-ai` | Native Gemini API format | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` |
| `tokenlab-minimax` | `anthropic-messages` | Native MiniMax routing | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` |

> Warning: Use the `/v1` suffix only for `openai-completions` and `openai-responses`.
>
> Native providers such as `anthropic-messages` and `google-generative-ai` should use `https://api.tokenlab.sh` without `/v1`, otherwise OpenClaw may construct the wrong provider path.

## Prerequisites

- A self-hosted OpenClaw instance
- For OpenClaw **2026.9.4**, use Node.js `>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0` ([version requirements](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.4/package.json)). For other OpenClaw releases, check that release's requirements.
- A TokenLab API Key — [Get one here](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/api?tab=keys)

## Configuration

Edit your OpenClaw config:

- **Self-hosted**: `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`

Add TokenLab providers under `models.providers`:

Use the same profile, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` as the running Gateway. Back up the active configuration before merging. Put `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` in that instance’s trusted global `.env` or service environment; a terminal export or project `.env` alone may not reach the background Gateway. See [environment handling](https://docs.openclaw.ai/help/environment).

Back up the active configuration. Add only the TokenLab entry and preserve existing providers, accounts, default-model selection and permissions. If the name is already used, choose another name and update the commands. To undo setup, remove only your added entry or restore its previous backup.

```json5
{
  models: {
    mode: "merge",
    providers: {
      tokenlab: {
        api: "openai-completions",
        baseUrl: "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1",
        apiKey: "${TOKENLAB_API_KEY}",
        models: [
          { id: "gpt-5.6-terra", name: "GPT-5.6 Terra" },
          { id: "deepseek-reasoner", name: "DeepSeek Reasoner" },
          { id: "qwen3-coder-flash", name: "Qwen 3 Coder Flash" }
        ]
      },
      "tokenlab-responses": {
        api: "openai-responses",
        baseUrl: "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1",
        apiKey: "${TOKENLAB_API_KEY}",
        models: [
          { id: "gpt-5.6-terra", name: "GPT-5.6 Terra (Responses)" },
          { id: "gpt-5.2", name: "GPT-5.2 (Responses)" }
        ]
      },
      "tokenlab-claude": {
        api: "anthropic-messages",
        baseUrl: "https://api.tokenlab.sh",
        apiKey: "${TOKENLAB_API_KEY}",
        models: [
          { id: "claude-sonnet-5", name: "Claude Sonnet 5" },
          { id: "claude-opus-5", name: "Claude Opus 5" }
        ]
      },
      "tokenlab-gemini": {
        api: "google-generative-ai",
        baseUrl: "https://api.tokenlab.sh",
        apiKey: "${TOKENLAB_API_KEY}",
        models: [
          { id: "gemini-3.5-flash", name: "Gemini 3.5 Flash" },
          { id: "gemini-2.5-pro", name: "Gemini 2.5 Pro" }
        ]
      },
      "tokenlab-minimax": {
        api: "anthropic-messages",
        baseUrl: "https://api.tokenlab.sh",
        apiKey: "${TOKENLAB_API_KEY}",
        models: [
          { id: "minimax-m3", name: "MiniMax M3" }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> Info: All 5 providers use the **same API Key**. You only need one TokenLab account.

> Info: The `models` arrays above only show common examples. Add more model IDs to each provider as needed.

## Using Models

OpenClaw still references models with the `provider/model` format:

For **OpenClaw 2026.9.4**, select the model only for the current session with `-s`. Keep `agents.defaults.model`, agent defaults and permissions unchanged. Use `/model default -s` to return this session to its configured default.

```text
/model tokenlab-claude/claude-sonnet-5 -s
/model default -s
```

### Model Examples

| Provider | Model reference | Description |
|----------|-----------------|-------------|
| `tokenlab` | `tokenlab/gpt-5.6-terra` | OpenAI-compatible route |
| `tokenlab-responses` | `tokenlab-responses/gpt-5.6-terra` | Responses API route |
| `tokenlab-claude` | `tokenlab-claude/claude-sonnet-5` | Native Claude Messages route |
| `tokenlab-gemini` | `tokenlab-gemini/gemini-3.5-flash` | Native Gemini route |
| `tokenlab-minimax` | `tokenlab-minimax/minimax-m3` | Native MiniMax route |

Browse all available models at [tokenlab.sh/models](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models).

## When to Use Which Provider

- `tokenlab`: default choice for most general-purpose agent and chat use cases.
- `tokenlab-responses`: use when your OpenClaw workflow explicitly depends on OpenAI Responses semantics.
- `tokenlab-claude`: use when you want Claude's native Messages behavior.
- `tokenlab-gemini`: use when you want Gemini-native request/response formatting or existing Gemini-style integrations.
- `tokenlab-minimax`: use when you want MiniMax on its native route.

If you do not need Gemini-native behavior, you can still call Gemini models through `tokenlab/gemini-*` on the OpenAI-compatible route.

## Common Mistakes

#### Still using the old top-level providers array

Current OpenClaw docs use `models.providers`. If you keep the older top-level `providers` array format, OpenClaw may ignore the config or fail to resolve the provider prefixes as expected.

#### Forgetting /v1 on tokenlab-responses

`openai-responses` maps to TokenLab's `/v1/responses` path, so `tokenlab-responses` must use `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1`.

#### Adding /v1 to tokenlab-claude, tokenlab-gemini, or tokenlab-minimax

`anthropic-messages` and `google-generative-ai` should use `https://api.tokenlab.sh` without `/v1`. Adding `/v1` can produce incorrect request paths.

#### Does OpenClaw still support native Gemini?

Yes. Current OpenClaw documentation still includes the built-in `google` provider and also supports custom providers using `api: "google-generative-ai"`. So `tokenlab-gemini` remains a valid native Gemini route for OpenClaw users.

## Verify Setup

Restart that instance, then inspect its selected model and provider. `models status` without `--probe` does not make a model-call test. A live `--probe` or a chat message can consume tokens. Check a real reply against the matching TokenLab request before declaring the setup working. To restore, choose the previous model and remove only the TokenLab entries you added.

```bash
openclaw gateway restart
openclaw models status
```

Once OpenClaw is connected, these guides help you use TokenLab more effectively:

- [API Formats](/guides/api-formats) — understand the differences between OpenAI, Responses, Anthropic, and Gemini routes
- [IDE / SDK Compatibility](/guides/ide-sdk-compatibility) — see when `/v1/responses` is the better fit
- [Error Handling](/guides/error-handling) — learn common failure modes and recovery patterns
- [Models Overview](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models) — browse model IDs before wiring them into agents

### TokenLab MCP Server

> Give Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, and other MCP clients access to TokenLab models and APIs

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/tokenlab-mcp-server

## Choose what your agent needs

- MCP adds TokenLab API tools to a compatible client. Start with the key-free `catalog` setup below.
- The [TokenLab Skill](/integrations/coding-agent-skill) installs integration instructions with `npx skills add`; it does not start an MCP server.

Both extend an existing agent. Changing its main model provider uses that client’s own setup guide.

## Let my agent set this up

Copy this task to an agent already running on your computer:

```text
Read this guide and choose MCP catalog tools or a Skill for my task:
https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/tokenlab-mcp-server
Check my installed version and active configuration first.
Preserve existing accounts, providers, permissions and other settings.
Back up local files and show proposed changes.
Have me enter any API key locally; never ask for, print or paste it in chat.
Check configuration loading first.
Explain any paid request test separately before running it.
```

The [TokenLab MCP Server](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-mcp-server) lets an MCP client browse current models and prices, send model requests, create media, work with files, and check async tasks.

Use the `catalog` profile to browse models and prices without an API key. Add `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` when the client should make paid model or media requests.

> Warning: Keep your TokenLab API key in the MCP server environment. Never paste it into a prompt or tool argument.

## Requirements

Install Node.js 18.17 or newer and make sure `npx` is available:

```bash
node --version
npx --version
```

The npm package runs locally over stdio. You do not need a global installation or a source checkout.

## Choose what the client can use

| Profile | API key | Includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | Not required | Model list, model details, prices, comparisons, and API overview |
| `core` | Required for paid calls | Common chat, media, audio, file, task, embedding, rerank, and translation tools |
| `full` | Required for paid calls | `core` plus additional developer APIs |

Start with `catalog` if you only want better model selection. Use `core` when the client should create content or call a model. `full` is for clients that genuinely need the larger tool set.

## Add the server

Back up the active configuration. Add only the TokenLab entry and preserve existing providers, accounts, default-model selection and permissions. If the name is already used, choose another name and update the commands. To undo setup, remove only your added entry or restore its previous backup.

#### Claude Code

Add the public catalog for your user account:

```bash
claude mcp add \
  --env TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE=catalog \
  --scope user \
  tokenlab -- \
  npx -y @tokenlabai/mcp-server@0.6.20
```

To use paid tools, replace the profile environment variable with `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` and store the key through your normal secret-management method. Use `--scope local` for one project. Never commit a real key in a shared `.mcp.json`.

#### Codex

```bash
codex mcp add \
  --env TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE=catalog \
  tokenlab -- \
  npx -y @tokenlabai/mcp-server@0.6.20
```

For paid tools, configure `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` in the server environment.

#### Cursor

Save this as `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for all projects or `.cursor/mcp.json` for one project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tokenlab": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@tokenlabai/mcp-server@0.6.20"],
      "env": {
        "TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE": "catalog"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### VS Code

Save this as `.vscode/mcp.json`, or add the same server through **MCP: Add Server**:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "tokenlab": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@tokenlabai/mcp-server@0.6.20"],
      "env": {
        "TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE": "catalog"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### Claude Desktop

Add this to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tokenlab": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@tokenlabai/mcp-server@0.6.20"],
      "env": {
        "TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE": "catalog"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### Other clients

Any local stdio MCP client can use these values:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Command | `npx` |
| Arguments | `-y`, `@tokenlabai/mcp-server@0.6.20` |
| Environment | `TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE=catalog` |

## Enable paid tools

Create an API key in [Console → API keys](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/api), then set both variables in the MCP server environment:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "TOKENLAB_API_KEY": "<TOKENLAB_API_KEY>",
    "TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE": "core"
  }
}
```

Use your client's secret input when it has one. If a real key appears in a shared file, screenshot, log, or shell history, revoke it and create a new key.

## Check the connection

Restart or reload the MCP client, approve the local server if prompted, and confirm that `tokenlab` is connected.

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp list

# Codex
codex mcp list
```

Ask the client to call `list_models`. A non-empty list confirms the package started and reached TokenLab. The `catalog` profile does not need an API key.

## Useful tools

Tool availability depends on the selected profile. Common tasks include:

- list models and read one model's capabilities
- read current TokenLab prices or compare several models
- send Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages, or Gemini requests
- create or edit images
- create video, music, 3D, speech, transcription, or translation
- upload and retrieve files
- create embeddings or rerank documents
- check and cancel supported async tasks

The client should ask for approval before a paid call when price or model choice has not already been confirmed.

## Async media

Video, music, and 3D tools return a task instead of a finished file. Image tools can return either a completed result or a task, depending on the model.

When a result includes an async `delivery`, call `get_task_status` with its task ID until the status is complete or failed. Do not create a second task because one status check timed out.

## Optional settings

| Variable | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TOKENLAB_API_BASE` | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` | Custom TokenLab API host; omit the trailing slash |
| `TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE` | `core` | `catalog`, `core`, or `full` |
| `TOKENLAB_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | `120000` | Request timeout in milliseconds |
| `TOKENLAB_MCP_MAX_FILE_BYTES` | `104857600` | Maximum local upload size per file |
| `TOKENLAB_ARTIFACT_DIR` | OS temporary directory | Where large downloaded files are saved |

Use the defaults unless your client or deployment has a specific requirement.

## Troubleshooting

#### The client cannot start the server

Run `node --version`, `npx --version`, and `npx -y @tokenlabai/mcp-server@0.6.20` in a terminal. A successful stdio server waits silently for MCP messages; press **Ctrl+C** after confirming it starts.

#### The server is connected but no tools appear

Restart the client and approve the local server. Confirm that the server and its tools are enabled in the client's MCP settings.

#### The model list is empty

Confirm that the machine can open `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/models`. If `TOKENLAB_API_BASE` is set, remove any trailing slash.

#### A paid tool returns an authentication error

Make sure `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` is in the MCP server environment, not in the prompt or tool arguments. Restart the client after changing it.

#### The client loads too many tools

Use `catalog` for model and price lookup, or `core` for common TokenLab calls. Choose `full` only when you need its additional APIs.

## Hosted model explorer

Clients that support Streamable HTTP can use the public model explorer at:

```text
https://tokenlab-model-explorer.vercel.app/mcp
```

Use the local npm server for paid API calls, local file uploads, or the `core` and `full` profiles.

## Links

- [TokenLab MCP page](https://tokenlab.sh/mcp)
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-mcp-server)
- [TokenLab API skill](/integrations/coding-agent-skill)
- [Model catalog](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models)
- [API quickstart](/quickstart)
