### DeepSeek Harness

> Configure a TokenLab model in Harness, verify a request, and choose MCP, Skills, or the provider bundle

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/deepseek-harness

## Choose the connection you need

To use TokenLab as the agent's main model, add a **custom provider** in the Harness Web UI. This works independently of the optional TokenLab provider bundle. Add [MCP tools](/integrations/tokenlab-mcp-server) for media and other APIs, or a [Skill](/integrations/coding-agent-skill) for API instructions; neither changes the main model by itself.

Harness is a developer preview. These Web UI steps were checked against the official documentation and the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.1.5-rc.1` package on September 16, 2026. The bundle instructions below target this version; check compatibility with other Harness releases separately.

## Give this task to your agent

```text
Read https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/deepseek-harness and check my installed version and operating system.
Confirm whether I need TokenLab as the main model, MCP tools, or API Skills.
Preserve existing accounts, provider configuration, and permissions; explain how to restore changed settings.
Keep API keys local; do not ask me to paste them into chat. I will enter the key locally and perform required UI steps.
Explain the cost of a small verification request. Only after I explicitly choose that test, help run it and match the TokenLab request record.
```

## Start Harness

Use the Node CLI on macOS, Linux, or Windows with a supported Node release; Node 24 LTS is a suitable starting point. From your project directory, run this in a terminal or PowerShell:

```bash
node --version
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.1 web
```

Open the local URL printed by the command. In a fresh Web UI, use **Choose workspace** to add and select your project directory before sending a message. These commands use the `web` profile; the Electron application's `desktop` profile is not managed by this CLI workflow. See the official [startup guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) and [Web UI guide](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/guide/quickstart).

## Configure one TokenLab provider

1. Open **Settings → Models → Add a custom provider**. Preserve any existing providers and permissions.
2. Enter a lowercase Provider ID, such as `tokenlab-chat`, and choose one protocol and its matching Base URL below. Each provider uses one protocol.
3. Enter your TokenLab API key in the local form. Harness stores UI-managed keys in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`; the settings document holds a reference. Do not send the key in chat or commit it.
4. Add one current model ID from [TokenLab Models](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models). Check its `tokenlab.accepted_request_formats` in the [model detail API](/api-reference/models/get-model), rather than guessing support from its name.
5. Save the provider, select its model, and start a **new session**. An existing session that has already sent a request retains its recorded model.

| Provider ID example | Harness API protocol | Base URL | Required public request format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tokenlab-chat` | `openai-completions` | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` | `openai_chat_completions` |
| `tokenlab-responses` | `openai-responses` | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` | `openai_responses` |
| `tokenlab-messages` | `anthropic-messages` | `https://api.tokenlab.sh` | `anthropic_messages` |

For a first text request, a currently available `gpt-4.1-mini` entry can use the Chat row. **Fetch available models → Add selected** can help populate a custom provider, but listing success does not verify protocol support or a billable request; save the provider afterward. Enter the ID manually if discovery is unavailable.

Harness does not offer a Gemini-native custom-provider protocol here. Use Chat only when that model's details list Chat Completions as an accepted request format. Image input and reasoning controls can need additional `settings.yaml` fields; follow [Harness provider configuration](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/guide/providers) and the selected model's supported fields before enabling them.

## Verify one small request

In the new session, send:

```text
Reply only with TOKENLAB_CONNECTION_OK. Do not use tools or modify files.
```

This request is billable. Check the reply and the matching model, time, and status in [TokenLab Requests](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests). Stop after this text check; testing three protocols or generating paid media is not required to establish the first connection. A model listing or MCP discovery alone does not validate the key's generation access.

## Optional: the TokenLab bundle

[`@tokenlabai/dsh-provider@0.1.3`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tokenlabai/dsh-provider/v/0.1.3) targets Harness `0.1.5-rc.1`. Use the native custom-provider steps above to configure one model, or install the bundle for its preset model routes and tools.

The bundle contains a **fixed snapshot of 124 public chat models checked on September 16, 2026**: Responses 23, Messages 9, and Chat 92. Each model appears on exactly one route. It pins `@tokenlabai/mcp-server@0.6.19` and includes the separate `tokenlab_wait_task` tool. Installing this version does not refresh the model catalog. Check IDs against the live catalog and add newer models through a custom provider when needed.

For an existing compatible Harness installation, first ensure `pnpm` is on `PATH`. Use the same `dsh` executable/version and profile for installation and startup; if you launch through `npx`, replace `dsh` below with that same versioned launcher:

```bash
dsh --version
pnpm --version
dsh plugin --profile web add --workspace-root @tokenlabai/dsh-provider@0.1.3
```

Before starting that profile, set the key in the launch environment or its `.env` file:

```dotenv
TOKENLAB_API_KEY=sk-your-tokenlab-key
```

Harness reads `.env` in the directory where you launch it and in `$DSH_HOME` (normally `~/.dsh`); an inherited environment variable takes precedence. Selecting a workspace later does not select a different `.env`. Keep that file out of git and restart after changing it. A key saved for a custom provider in the UI does not automatically supply this bundle's `TOKENLAB_API_KEY`.

Restart the same profile, then inspect its model and tool lists. For `headless`, install into and launch `headless` instead of `web`; installing into one profile does not configure the other.

Harness `0.1.5-rc.1` merges saved `llm-pi-ai.providers` by provider key. Providers with different keys coexist. Saved `tokenlab-responses`, `tokenlab-messages`, or `tokenlab-chat` entries override the corresponding bundled route; review those entries when upgrading an older catalog. Preserve the other providers and models in `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml`; do not replace the whole settings document with the Cordis patch.

Public model details identify reasoning capability but do not enumerate supported effort values per model. The bundle therefore leaves `reasoningEfforts` undeclared. Harness does not offer effort levels for these custom routes; this does not disable server-side reasoning. If you configure `reasoningEfforts` yourself, use only separately verified values on the model entry in its provider’s `models` list and preserve the other models. Reasoning capability alone does not establish support for `xhigh` or `max`.

The bundle defaults to `TOKENLAB_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE=core` with 31 MCP tools and `TOKENLAB_MCP_SCHEMA_MODE=portable`. Choose `catalog` for discovery only (6 tools), or `full` for all 80 tools, including additional response lifecycle, batch, Seedance asset/group, and worlds operations. The separate `tokenlab_wait_task` poller remains available in every profile and is not included in these MCP counts. `TOKENLAB_API_BASE` and `TOKENLAB_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` default to `https://api.tokenlab.sh`; `TOKENLAB_OPENAI_BASE_URL` defaults to `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1`.

For bundle media tools, inspect `delivery.mode`: consume `complete` output directly; pass an `async` result's `delivery.task_id` to `tokenlab_wait_task` and read its terminal `status`, `response`, and `result_urls`. A wait timeout is not a completed task. Keep approvals for billable or destructive tools. See [async tasks](/guides/async-jobs-polling).

To remove the bundle, use the same launcher and profile, then restart:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove --workspace-root @tokenlabai/dsh-provider
```

## If it fails

- **The composer is disabled:** select both a workspace and a model.
- **`MISSING_CREDENTIAL` or 401:** check the selected provider's credential. For bundle tools, check `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` in the launch environment; a UI-saved model key is a separate setting.
- **`UNKNOWN_MODEL` or a retired ID:** check the live catalog, configure the current exact ID, then create a new session. Reinstalling bundle `0.1.3` does not update its snapshot.
- **The URL is reachable but generation fails:** compare the protocol, Base URL, and model's accepted formats. Do not remove history, tools, or image input merely to turn an error into a successful check.
- **`dsh` or `pnpm` is missing:** use the versioned `npx` launcher above for Harness; install [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/installation) before using plugin commands. A plugin installation failure is not an API-key failure.

## MCP and Skills are separate choices

A manual custom provider does not install tools. Follow the [TokenLab MCP guide](/integrations/tokenlab-mcp-server) if you need callable API tools without the bundle, and check discovery before any generation.

For [TokenLab Skills](/integrations/coding-agent-skill), keep the complete skill folder at `.dsh/skills/tokenlab-api-integration/` under the project root, including `SKILL.md` and referenced files. Harness also discovers `.agents/skills/`. These instructions do not install a provider, MCP server, or key. The official [filesystem Skills reference](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/skill/skill-filesystem/README.md) defines the supported locations.

---

### GitHub Copilot CLI

> Connect GitHub Copilot CLI to TokenLab with BYOK

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/github-copilot-cli

## Overview

[GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/use-byok-models) can connect to any OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint. TokenLab works through Copilot CLI's BYOK environment variables.

## Install

With Node.js 22 or later, install through npm:

```bash
npm install -g @github/copilot@1.0.85
```

On macOS or Linux, you can alternatively use Homebrew:

```bash
brew install --cask copilot-cli
```

Verify the installation:

```bash
copilot --version
```

## Configure TokenLab

Set the provider variables before starting Copilot CLI:

Use the [Quickstart](/quickstart) terminal instructions for macOS, Linux, WSL, or Windows PowerShell to set `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` without putting the key in command history. Launch Copilot CLI from that terminal. For persistent use, use your local secret manager; do not append a plaintext key to your shell profile.

These variables apply only to this launch; your saved account, default model and permission settings stay in place. Launch normally without the variables to use your previous setup. Do not persist them in your shell profile.

#### macOS / Linux / WSL

```bash macOS / Linux / WSL
COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1 COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY="${TOKENLAB_API_KEY:?Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first}" copilot --model kimi-k3
```

#### Windows PowerShell

```powershell Windows PowerShell
if (-not $env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY) { throw 'Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first' }
$previous = @{}
$previous['COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE', 'Process')
$previous['COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL', 'Process')
$previous['COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY', 'Process')
try {
  $env:COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE = 'openai'
  $env:COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL = 'https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1'
  $env:COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY = $env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY
  copilot --model kimi-k3
} finally {
  foreach ($name in $previous.Keys) {
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable($name, $previous[$name], 'Process')
  }
}
```

| Variable | TokenLab value |
|---|---|
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE` | `openai` |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY` | Your TokenLab API key |
| `COPILOT_MODEL` | A live model ID, for example `kimi-k3` |

GitHub requires the selected model to support both streaming and tool calling. `kimi-k3` exposes tool use and a context window larger than GitHub's recommended 128K minimum.

## Verify

Inside Copilot CLI, ask for a read-only action first, such as:

```text
Inspect this repository and summarize its top-level structure. Do not modify files.
```

You can also inspect provider help or switch the model for the current session:

```bash
copilot help providers
```

## Troubleshooting

#### Authentication failed

Confirm `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY` contains an active TokenLab key and restart `copilot` after changing environment variables.

#### Model not found

Use the exact ID from the [live TokenLab model catalog](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models). Do not add a provider prefix to `kimi-k3`.

#### Tool calling or streaming error

Copilot CLI rejects models without both capabilities. Choose a tool-capable chat model such as `kimi-k3`.

> Warning: Do not commit API keys to shell scripts or dotfiles tracked by Git. Rotate any key that was exposed in terminal history, screenshots, or logs.

Saving settings or listing models does not verify a key or a completed request. A prompt uses TokenLab balance. Check the reply and its matching [request record](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests) before trying tools; auxiliary requests may also be billed.

### Cursor

> Configure TokenLab for supported Cursor chat models, verify the connection, and add MCP or Skills separately

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/cursor

## What this connection does

Use TokenLab for supported chat requests in the **Cursor desktop editor** on macOS, Windows, or Linux. Cursor documents OpenAI BYOK support for standard, non-reasoning chat models; Tab completion still uses Cursor's models. An OpenAI Base URL override does not turn Cursor into a client for every TokenLab model or protocol. See [Cursor's API-key limits](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/api-keys).

If you only need TokenLab image, video, or other API tools, keep your current chat provider and add [MCP](/integrations/tokenlab-mcp-server) instead. A [Skill](/integrations/coding-agent-skill) teaches the agent how to use the APIs; it does not change the chat provider.

## Give this task to your agent

```text
Read https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/cursor and check my installed version and operating system.
Confirm whether I need TokenLab as the main model, MCP tools, or API Skills.
Preserve existing accounts, provider configuration, and permissions; explain how to restore changed settings.
Keep API keys local; do not ask me to paste them into chat. I will enter the key locally and perform required UI steps.
Explain the cost of a small verification request. Only after I explicitly choose that test, help run it and match the TokenLab request record.
```

## Open the correct settings

1. Install or update the desktop editor from [Cursor Downloads](https://cursor.com/downloads). This guide does not configure Cursor CLI or Cloud Agents.
2. Open **Cursor Settings** from the command palette, or press `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + J`. `Cmd/Ctrl + ,` opens the general editor settings instead.
3. Open **Models** and note your existing OpenAI key and Base URL configuration so you can restore it. Keep other provider settings intact.
4. In **OpenAI API Key**, enter your TokenLab key locally and save it. Do not paste the key into an agent conversation or commit it to a project.
5. Enable **Override OpenAI Base URL** and enter:

```text
https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1
```

Cursor sends BYOK requests through its backend for prompt assembly; this is not a direct connection from your editor to TokenLab.

## Select a supported model

Copy the exact model ID from the current [TokenLab catalog](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models), and check that Cursor accepts it through its OpenAI BYOK path. A model being listed as chat on TokenLab does not establish Cursor compatibility.

For an initial text check, `gpt-4.1-mini` is an example of a non-reasoning OpenAI chat model; confirm it is still available before using it. Enable the existing entry in **Models**, or use **Add model** if it is absent, then select that exact model in the chat picker. Do not duplicate a built-in model under a different spelling, and do not assume Claude or Gemini entries use the OpenAI override. [Cursor's custom-model guidance](https://forum.cursor.com/t/add-custom-model-fail-no-models-available/163488) explains these routing limits.

## Verify one small request

Start a new chat with the selected model and send:

```text
Reply only with TOKENLAB_CONNECTION_OK. Do not use tools or modify files.
```

This is a billable model request. Check both the reply and the matching model, time, and status in [TokenLab Requests](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests). A saved key, a visible model, or a reply without a matching TokenLab request does not confirm this route.

## If it fails

- **The model is missing or rejected:** check the exact ID and Cursor's current BYOK support. Use an existing built-in entry when available; restarting alone cannot make an unsupported model compatible.
- **Authentication fails:** re-enter the TokenLab key in the OpenAI field and check the Base URL. A balance or quota error is separate from an invalid key; follow the returned error and the corresponding TokenLab request.
- **No TokenLab request appears:** confirm the selected model and override, then inspect Cursor's error. Tab completion and other Cursor-managed features are not a connection test.
- **Another provider stops working:** restore the previous OpenAI settings or disable the override, then start a new chat. Avoid changing unrelated provider keys to repair this route.

## Add tools or instructions separately

[TokenLab MCP](/integrations/tokenlab-mcp-server) adds callable tools. Configure it through Cursor's MCP settings or `.cursor/mcp.json`; first check tool discovery, then deliberately run any billable generation you need. Installing MCP does not replace the main chat model.

[TokenLab Skills](/integrations/coding-agent-skill) supply API instructions. For a project-local installation, keep the complete skill directory at `.cursor/skills/tokenlab-api-integration/`, including `SKILL.md` and its referenced files. Check **Customize → Skills** for discovery. Skills do not supply a key or install an MCP server. See the official [MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp) and [Skills](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) guides for your Cursor version.

### Cline

> Configure Cline to use TokenLab models

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/cline

## Overview

[Cline](https://docs.cline.bot/provider-config/openai-compatible) can use TokenLab through its OpenAI-compatible settings.

## Install

Install **Cline** from your editor's extension marketplace, then open the Cline panel. Cline supports VS Code, Cursor, VSCodium, Windsurf, Antigravity, and JetBrains IDEs.

## Configure TokenLab

Save the current provider, model and connection settings locally before editing. These controls change the active model selection; restore your previous values when finished. Keep signed-in accounts and tool permissions unchanged. Do not overwrite another OpenAI-compatible connection without a restorable backup.

1. Click the gear icon in the Cline panel.
2. Set **API Provider** to **OpenAI Compatible**.
3. Enter the following values:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Base URL | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| API Key | Your TokenLab API key |
| Model ID | `kimi-k3` |

4. Click **Verify**.

For the `kimi-k3` example, Cline's optional model configuration can use:

| Capability | Value |
|---|---|
| Context / input limit | `1048576` |
| Max output tokens | `131072` |
| Image support | Enabled |

> Note: The model catalog changes over time. Use the [live TokenLab model catalog](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models) when selecting another model instead of copying a stale list.

## Verify

After **Verify** succeeds, send a small read-only task before allowing edits:

```text
List the files in this workspace and explain which one is the application entry point. Do not edit anything.
```

Saving settings or listing models does not verify a key or a completed request. A prompt uses TokenLab balance. Check the reply and its matching [request record](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests) before trying tools; auxiliary requests may also be billed.

## Troubleshooting

#### Invalid API key

Re-copy the key from the TokenLab dashboard and confirm it is active.

#### Model not found

Enter the model ID exactly as shown by TokenLab, for example `kimi-k3`, without `kimi/` or another provider prefix.

#### Connection error

Confirm the Base URL ends in `/v1`. Do not enter `/chat/completions` in Cline's Base URL field.

### Claude Code

> Use TokenLab with Anthropic's Claude Code CLI

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/claude-code

## Let my agent set this up

Copy this task to an agent already running on your computer:

```text
Read this guide and help me connect Claude Code to TokenLab:
https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/claude-code
Check my installed version and active configuration first.
Preserve existing accounts, providers, permissions and other settings.
Back up local files and show proposed changes.
Have me enter any API key locally; never ask for, print or paste it in chat.
Check configuration loading first.
Explain any paid request test separately before running it.
```

## Overview

[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) can use a TokenLab API key and the TokenLab Messages API for Claude models.

## Installation

Anthropic now recommends the native installer. The npm package still works, but Anthropic has deprecated that installation method.

#### macOS / Linux / WSL

```bash macOS / Linux / WSL
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

#### Windows

```powershell Windows
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

If you specifically need the npm package, use:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.263
```

> Warning: Do not use `sudo npm install -g` for Claude Code.

## Configuration

Use the [Quickstart](/quickstart) terminal instructions for macOS, Linux, WSL, or Windows PowerShell to set `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` without putting the key in command history. Launch Claude Code from that terminal. For persistent use, use your local secret manager; do not append a plaintext key to your shell profile.

These variables apply only to this launch; your saved account, default model and permission settings stay in place. Launch normally without the variables to use your previous setup. Do not persist them in your shell profile.

This session path uses Claude Code **2.1.263** and Bearer authentication through `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. Keep the Base URL without `/v1`. Existing settings-file `env` values, credential helpers, cloud-provider switches or managed policies can affect authentication; inspect them before launch. If they conflict, use the setup helper below instead of deleting account data or weakening policies. Check `/status` for the selected model and permissions.

#### macOS / Linux / WSL

```bash macOS / Linux / WSL
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.tokenlab.sh ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${TOKENLAB_API_KEY:?Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first}" ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6
```

#### Windows PowerShell

```powershell Windows PowerShell
if (-not $env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY) { throw 'Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first' }
$previous = @{}
$previous['ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL', 'Process')
$previous['ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN', 'Process')
$previous['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'Process')
try {
  $env:ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = 'https://api.tokenlab.sh'
  $env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = $env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY
  $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = ''
  claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6
} finally {
  foreach ($name in $previous.Keys) {
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable($name, $previous[$name], 'Process')
  }
}
```

Optional: the [reversible Claude Code setup helper](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-skills/blob/247bb17c53754c8288d2d5cb00824fbd9f32899b/skills/tokenlab-api-integration/references/claude_setup.md) provides preview, apply and original-file restoration with Python 3.11+. TokenLab Skills plugin **0.1.2** includes these scripts; a standalone Skill installation can also be used after updating to a version that contains them. For an existing plugin or standalone Skill installation, follow the [README update instructions](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-skills/blob/247bb17c53754c8288d2d5cb00824fbd9f32899b/README.md#update-an-existing-installation) and confirm the script is present. The manual configuration here remains usable without the helper.

Saving settings or listing models does not verify a key or a completed request. A prompt uses TokenLab balance. Check the reply and its matching [request record](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests) before trying tools; auxiliary requests may also be billed.

## Usage

After configuration, use Claude Code normally:

```bash
# Start an interactive session
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.tokenlab.sh ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${TOKENLAB_API_KEY:?Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first}" ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6

# Run a single command
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.tokenlab.sh ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${TOKENLAB_API_KEY:?Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first}" ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6 "Explain this code" < main.py
```

Verify the installation if needed:

```bash
claude --version
claude doctor
```

## Choose a model

Copy a current Claude model ID from the [Models page](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models), then pass it with `--model`:

```bash
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.tokenlab.sh ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${TOKENLAB_API_KEY:?Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first}" ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6 "Review this PR"
```

## Extended Thinking

For complex reasoning tasks, use models with extended thinking:

```bash
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.tokenlab.sh ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${TOKENLAB_API_KEY:?Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first}" ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= claude --model claude-opus-4-6 "Design a microservices architecture for..."
```

## Troubleshooting

#### Connection errors

Verify the base URL is exactly `https://api.tokenlab.sh` (no `/v1` suffix for Anthropic-style requests).

#### Invalid API key

Ensure your TokenLab API key starts with `sk-` and has sufficient balance.

#### Model not found

Check the model name is correct. Use `claude-sonnet-4-6` format.

### Codex CLI

> Configure OpenAI Codex CLI to use TokenLab API

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/codex-cli

## Let my agent set this up

Copy this task to an agent already running on your computer:

```text
Read this guide and help me connect Codex CLI to TokenLab:
https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/codex-cli
Check my installed version and active configuration first.
Preserve existing accounts, providers, permissions and other settings.
Back up local files and show proposed changes.
Have me enter any API key locally; never ask for, print or paste it in chat.
Check configuration loading first.
Explain any paid request test separately before running it.
```

## Overview

Codex CLI can connect to TokenLab through `/v1/responses`. The selected model must list `openai_responses` in `tokenlab.accepted_request_formats`; features can vary by model.

Remote compaction uses `POST /v1/responses/compact`. Codex sends the current session model in `body.model`, so that model must also support Responses. Do not configure `/v1/compact`.

## System Requirements

Use the [official CLI installation guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli) for macOS, Linux or Windows. Native Windows and WSL are separate environments; follow the [Windows guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox). The npm command below is one installation option, not a requirement for native binaries.

## Installation

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex@0.149.0
```

Verify installation:

```bash
codex --version
```

## Configuration

### Step 1: Set API Key

Use the [Quickstart](/quickstart) terminal instructions for macOS, Linux, WSL, or Windows PowerShell to set `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` without putting the key in command history. Launch Codex from that terminal. For persistent use, use your local secret manager; do not append a plaintext key to your shell profile.

### Step 2: Configure tokenlab.config.toml

Use a separate `tokenlab.config.toml` in your active `CODEX_HOME` (normally `~/.codex`) with Codex **0.149.0**. Create it only if the name is unused, or back it up before editing an existing TokenLab profile. The profile below is loaded explicitly with `codex --profile tokenlab`; it leaves the default `config.toml`, `auth.json`, accounts and permission policies unchanged. Do not use a legacy `[profiles.tokenlab]` table. Start without the profile to return to your ordinary setup. See the [official profile configuration](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-advanced#profiles).

```toml
model_provider = "tokenlab"
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"

[model_providers.tokenlab]
env_key = "TOKENLAB_API_KEY"
name = "TokenLab"
base_url = "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
supports_websockets = true
websocket_connect_timeout_ms = 15000
```

This WebSocket mode is a Responses-over-WebSocket bridge for Codex clients. It accepts only official `response.create` events; `stream` is implicit, and `background` and `response.cancel` are not available on this transport. It is not the OpenAI Realtime API and does not accept `session.update`, `conversation.item.*`, `input_audio_buffer.*`, binary audio, or nested Realtime `response.create.response` envelopes.

> Note: Create the chosen configuration file if it does not exist. After editing it, start a new session with the matching command below.

Current Codex uses `wire_api = "responses"`. Do not configure `chat/completions`. Keep `requires_openai_auth` unset or false for this custom provider so `env_key` is used.

> Note: Responses requests are not converted to Chat Completions. Optional and future fields depend on the selected model.

## Basic Usage

**Start interactive mode:**

```bash
codex --profile tokenlab
```

**Direct command:**

```bash
codex --profile tokenlab "Fix the bug in main.py line 42"
```

**Specify model:**

```bash
codex --profile tokenlab -m gpt-5.6-sol "Build a REST API server"
```

## Choose a model

Use a model that currently lists `openai_responses` in `tokenlab.accepted_request_formats`. Compare candidates on your own coding tasks and check current prices on the [Models page](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models).

## Interactive Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/help` | Display help |
| `/exit` or `Ctrl+C` | Exit |
| `/clear` | Clear conversation |
| `/status` | Show the active model, permissions, and token usage |
| `/model <name>` | Switch model |

## Verify Configuration

Check whether the environment variable is set without printing its value. This check does not validate the key:

```bash
if [ -n "${TOKENLAB_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' 'TOKENLAB_API_KEY is set'
else
  printf '%s\n' 'TOKENLAB_API_KEY is not set'
fi
```

Start Codex and run `/status` to check the active model and permissions. If you use a profile, start that same profile. See the [official status command](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli#inspect-the-session-with-status).

When you are ready to make a real request, run the command below. It uses your TokenLab balance. Check the reply and the matching record in [Requests](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests); an environment check or successful startup alone does not prove a request succeeded.

```bash
codex --profile tokenlab "Reply only with OK. Do not use tools or modify files."
```

## Common Use Cases

**Code review:**

```bash
git diff | codex --profile tokenlab "Review these code changes"
```

**Generate commit messages:**

```bash
git diff --staged | codex --profile tokenlab "Generate a commit message for these changes"
```

**Fix errors:**

```bash
codex --profile tokenlab "Fix the TypeScript errors in src/components/"
```

**Explain code:**

```bash
cat main.py | codex --profile tokenlab "Explain what this code does"
```

## Troubleshooting

#### Connection Error

- Verify `base_url` in tokenlab.config.toml is exactly `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1`
- Check network connectivity
- Ensure no proxy interference

#### Authentication Failed

After upgrading to Codex 0.149.0 or later, `API_KEY_REQUIRED` or `401 Unauthorized` can occur if a custom provider relies only on `auth.json` while `requires_openai_auth` is unset or `false`. This guide reads the key from `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` through `env_key` and does not rely on `auth.json`. Keep `requires_openai_auth` unset or `false`; this setup does not require changing it to `true` or overwriting `auth.json`.

- Verify that the active configuration or profile contains `env_key = "TOKENLAB_API_KEY"`. If you saved the settings in `tokenlab.config.toml`, launch with `codex --profile tokenlab`.
- Verify that `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` is set in the terminal used to launch Codex, then restart Codex from that terminal.
- Check that the key starts with `sk-`
- Ensure the key is active in TokenLab dashboard

#### Model Not Found

- Check model name matches exactly
- Verify model availability at [tokenlab.sh/en/models](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models)

#### Responses-native field rejected

- Optional `/v1/responses` fields depend on the selected model
- If you see `unsupported_request_field`, remove that field or switch to a workflow that does not depend on it

#### /compact or auto-compact fails

- Codex CLI calls `POST /v1/responses/compact`, not `/v1/compact`
- The compaction request uses the current session `model`, so that model must be available on the Responses path
- Keep `wire_api = "responses"` and `base_url = "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1"`

### WorkBuddy

> Add TokenLab as a custom model provider in WorkBuddy

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/workbuddy

## Let my agent set this up

Copy this task to an agent already running on your computer:

```text
Read this guide and help me connect WorkBuddy to TokenLab:
https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/workbuddy
Check my installed version and active configuration first.
Preserve existing accounts, providers, permissions and other settings.
Back up local files and show proposed changes.
Have me enter any API key locally; never ask for, print or paste it in chat.
Check configuration loading first.
Explain any paid request test separately before running it.
```

## Overview

[WorkBuddy](https://www.codebuddy.cn/docs/workbuddy/From-Beginner-to-Expert-Guide/Function-Description/Model) can add TokenLab through its visual custom-model editor.

## Configure TokenLab

1. Open **Settings → Model**.
2. Add a model and select **Custom** as the provider.
3. Enter the following values:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Endpoint URL | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| API Key | Your TokenLab API key |
| Model name | A current TokenLab chat model ID |
| Custom Protocol | **Off** |

> Warning: Keep **Custom Protocol** off. In standard mode WorkBuddy validates the base URL and appends `/chat/completions`. If you turn it on while entering only `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1`, requests are sent to the wrong path.

## Advanced model settings

Choose capability flags and context/output limits from the selected model’s current TokenLab details. Do not enable image input or reasoning for every model, and do not copy a 1M/128K limit to a different model. Use the model ID exactly as shown by TokenLab.

Saving and selecting a model confirms only local configuration. A text or tool task uses TokenLab balance; compare its reply with the matching [request record](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests). To undo setup, select your previous model and remove only the TokenLab entry in the editor.

## Verify

Start with a small task that exercises both text generation and a safe tool read:

```text
Inspect this folder, list its top-level files, and summarize what the project does. Do not modify files.
```

## Troubleshooting

#### 404 or route not found

Confirm the endpoint is `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` and **Custom Protocol** is off. Do not paste `/chat/completions` when standard mode is selected.

#### Model not found

Copy the exact model ID from TokenLab and check that it supports Chat Completions and tools.

#### Agent replies but cannot use tools

Enable **Tool calling** and make sure the selected TokenLab model advertises tool-use support.

> Warning: Screenshots of the model dialog can reveal endpoints or API keys. Mask credentials before sharing them and rotate any exposed key.

The official desktop app is available for macOS and Windows. Use the [official model editor](https://www.codebuddy.cn/docs/workbuddy/From-Beginner-to-Expert-Guide/Function-Description/Model); this guide does not assume a Linux build or a writable configuration-file schema.

MCP and Skills have separate installation paths: [API tools](/integrations/tokenlab-mcp-server) and [integration instructions](/integrations/coding-agent-skill). They do not change WorkBuddy’s main model.

### Hermes Agent

> Connect Hermes Agent to TokenLab

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/hermes-agent

Use TokenLab as a named model provider in Hermes while keeping your existing accounts and tool permissions.

## Let my agent set this up

Copy this task to an agent already running on your computer:

```text
Read this guide and help me connect Hermes to TokenLab:
https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/hermes-agent
Check my installed version and active configuration first.
Preserve existing accounts, providers, permissions and other settings.
Back up local files and show proposed changes.
Have me enter any API key locally; never ask for, print or paste it in chat.
Check configuration loading first.
Explain any paid request test separately before running it.
```

## Install or check Hermes

Follow the [official installation guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/installation). It offers desktop installers for Apple Silicon macOS and Windows, and a CLI path for Linux and native Windows. Check the requirements for your system; skip installation if Hermes is already installed.

## Optional: reversible setup

Use the Hermes helper included in TokenLab Skills **0.1.3** for official Hermes **0.21.3**. It previews and backs up the change, adds only a named provider, and preserves YAML comments, accounts, the default model and permissions. Read the [setup reference](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-skills/blob/900de0c4e296c0d2ed00b5d842815ed89c403503/skills/tokenlab-api-integration/references/hermes_setup.md) first.

Set `SKILL_DIR` to the installed `tokenlab-api-integration` folder and `HERMES_PYTHON` to the Python in the Hermes installation shown by `hermes --version`: `venv/bin/python` on macOS/Linux or `venv\Scripts\python.exe` on Windows. PowerShell uses `$SkillDir` and `$HermesPython`. Use that existing environment; the helper does not install global Python packages.

```bash
"$HERMES_PYTHON" "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/configure_hermes.py" --model gpt-5.6-luna
"$HERMES_PYTHON" "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/configure_hermes.py" --model gpt-5.6-luna --apply
```

```powershell
& $HermesPython "$SkillDir/scripts/configure_hermes.py" --model gpt-5.6-luna
& $HermesPython "$SkillDir/scripts/configure_hermes.py" --model gpt-5.6-luna --apply
```

After applying, skip the manual merge below. Follow the helper’s printed home and loading commands; it detects `active_profile`. Configuration inspection does not validate the key. Preview restoration with `--restore`, then add `--apply` to restore the original bytes. Conflicts, later edits, managed settings and WSL stop automatic setup; retain those settings and use the manual route.

## Configure a named provider

Find the active Hermes directory: `HERMES_HOME` when set, otherwise `~/.hermes` (Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`). Back up `config.yaml`, then merge the following entries without replacing other settings. The example uses Chat Completions; choose a current model that supports this format and tool calling.

Back up the active configuration. Add only the TokenLab entry and preserve existing providers, accounts, default-model selection and permissions. If the name is already used, choose another name and update the commands. To undo setup, remove only your added entry or restore its previous backup.

```yaml
providers:
  tokenlab:
    api: https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1
    key_env: TOKENLAB_API_KEY
    transport: chat_completions
    default_model: gpt-5.6-luna
```

Create a key in [API keys](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/api?tab=keys). Enter it locally as `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` in the Hermes directory’s `.env` or in the environment of the process that starts Hermes. Never paste the key into a conversation or put it in the provider YAML.

## Check configuration, then make a request

Check the added provider with `hermes config get providers.tokenlab.api`; it should show `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1`. Keep the existing `model` section unchanged. Start a new session with the explicit provider and model below; launch normally without these flags to use your previous default. Configuration inspection does not validate the key.

```bash
hermes chat --provider custom:tokenlab --model gpt-5.6-luna
```

When ready to spend TokenLab balance, send a short text request. Check the response and its matching record in [Requests](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests). Only then try a read-only tool task. Auxiliary models and optional tools can have separate providers or keys.

## Restore or troubleshoot

If the provider is unknown, check the installed version and the [current provider format](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers). For authentication errors, check the local environment and key status without printing the key. To undo setup, restore the previous model selection and remove only the TokenLab entries you added.

MCP and Skills are separate extensions: use the [MCP guide](/integrations/tokenlab-mcp-server) for API tools or the [Skill guide](/integrations/coding-agent-skill) for integration guidance. Neither is required to select this provider.

### Kilo Code

> Connect Kilo Code and Kilo CLI to TokenLab

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/kilo-code

## Overview

[Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/docs/ai-providers/openai-compatible) supports custom OpenAI-compatible providers in its VS Code extension and Kilo CLI. Both clients share the same provider and model configuration.

## Install

For VS Code, search for **Kilo Code** in Extensions and install the pre-release channel. Kilo documents that channel as the current stable, recommended extension.

For the CLI, run:

```bash
npm install -g @kilocode/cli@7.7.2
kilo --version
```

## Configure in the UI

Save the current provider, model and connection settings locally before editing. These controls change the active model selection; restore your previous values when finished. Keep signed-in accounts and tool permissions unchanged. Do not overwrite another OpenAI-compatible connection without a restorable backup.

1. Open Kilo Code **Settings → Providers**.
2. Scroll down and click **Custom provider**.
3. Use these values:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Provider ID | `tokenlab` |
| Display name | `TokenLab` |
| Provider API | **OpenAI Compatible** |
| Base URL | `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` |
| API key | Your TokenLab API key |
| Model | Select or add `kimi-k3` |

Kilo automatically queries TokenLab's `/v1/models` endpoint after the Base URL and key are entered. Click **Submit**, then choose `tokenlab/kimi-k3` in the model picker.

## Configure the CLI

Use the [Quickstart](/quickstart) terminal instructions for macOS, Linux, WSL, or Windows PowerShell to set `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` without putting the key in command history. Launch Kilo from that terminal. For persistent use, use your local secret manager; do not append a plaintext key to your shell profile.

Before starting Kilo **7.7.2**, back up the active global configuration and check `permission.bash`. This version migrates an existing configuration without that explicit rule to `bash: "allow"`, even when `permission["*"]` is `deny`. Preserve your current shell rule explicitly in the global file: if the existing wildcard rule is `deny`, merge `"bash": "deny"` into the existing `permission` object. Keep other rules intact. The separate provider file below does not prevent this client migration.

Create a separate `~/.config/kilo/tokenlab.jsonc` file with the configuration below. If `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, use `kilo/tokenlab.jsonc` under that directory. Keep the normal `kilo.json` / `kilo.jsonc`, accounts, default model and permissions unchanged: this separate file is loaded only for an invocation that selects it with `KILO_CONFIG`. If the file or provider name already belongs to another setup, choose a different file/name and adjust the commands.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://app.kilo.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "tokenlab": {
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "{env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY}",
        "baseURL": "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1"
      },
      "models": {
        "kimi-k3": {
          "name": "Kimi K3",
          "tool_call": true,
          "reasoning": true,
          "modalities": {
            "input": [
              "text",
              "image"
            ],
            "output": [
              "text"
            ]
          },
          "limit": {
            "context": 1048576,
            "output": 131072
          }
        }
      },
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "TokenLab"
    }
  }
}
```

#### macOS / Linux / WSL

```bash macOS / Linux / WSL
KILO_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/kilo/tokenlab.jsonc" kilo models tokenlab
KILO_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/kilo/tokenlab.jsonc" kilo --model tokenlab/kimi-k3
```

#### Windows PowerShell

```powershell Windows PowerShell
$previous = @{}
$previous['KILO_CONFIG'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('KILO_CONFIG', 'Process')
try {
  $env:KILO_CONFIG = (Join-Path $(if ($env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME) { $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME } else { Join-Path $HOME '.config' }) 'kilo/tokenlab.jsonc')
  kilo models tokenlab
  kilo --model tokenlab/kimi-k3
} finally {
  foreach ($name in $previous.Keys) {
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable($name, $previous[$name], 'Process')
  }
}
```

Saving settings or listing models does not verify a key or a completed request. A prompt uses TokenLab balance. Check the reply and its matching [request record](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests) before trying tools; auxiliary requests may also be billed.

## Troubleshooting

#### Models do not appear

Confirm the Base URL ends in `/v1`, the key is active, and `kilo models` lists the configured provider. Add `kimi-k3` manually if model discovery is unavailable.

#### Context compaction does not run

Custom models need explicit `limit.context` and `limit.output` values. Keep the limits aligned with TokenLab's current model metadata.

#### The model cannot edit or run tools

Confirm `tool_call` is `true`, then review Kilo's permission settings for the current project.

### Gemini CLI

> Configure Google Gemini CLI to use TokenLab API

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/gemini-cli

## Overview

Gemini CLI **0.60.0** documents `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` for API-key authentication. Use TokenLab’s Gemini-native endpoint with a current model that supports `gemini_generate_content`. See the [official configuration reference](https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/configuration/) and [authentication guide](https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/). This setup does not route a Google subscription through TokenLab.

## Installation

```bash
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@0.60.0
gemini --version
```

## Configuration

Use the [Quickstart](/quickstart) terminal instructions for macOS, Linux, WSL, or Windows PowerShell to set `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` without putting the key in command history. Launch Gemini CLI from that terminal. For persistent use, use your local secret manager; do not append a plaintext key to your shell profile.

Keep your current Google login and configuration. For a separate TokenLab launch, choose an unused configuration root such as `~/.gemini-tokenlab` (`$HOME` on PowerShell) and create its `.gemini` directory. Copy your existing `.gemini/settings.json` and any policy files needed by your setup into the corresponding locations, preserving permissions, sandbox and unrelated settings. In that copy only, merge the following authentication field; create a settings file if none exists. Do not copy OAuth caches or clear your original credentials. Follow managed authentication policy instead of overriding it.

```json
{
  "security": {
    "auth": {
      "selectedType": "gemini-api-key"
    }
  }
}
```

## Usage

The launch below uses `~/.gemini-tokenlab/.gemini/settings.json`. Adjust the path if you chose another root. Approve the working directory through Gemini’s normal trust prompt; keep existing tool-approval policies. The model is selected explicitly for this session.

#### macOS / Linux / WSL

```bash macOS / Linux / WSL
GEMINI_CLI_HOME="$HOME/.gemini-tokenlab" GEMINI_API_KEY="${TOKENLAB_API_KEY:?Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first}" GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL=https://api.tokenlab.sh gemini --model gemini-3.5-flash
```

#### Windows PowerShell

```powershell Windows PowerShell
if (-not $env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY) { throw 'Set TOKENLAB_API_KEY first' }
$previous = @{}
$previous['GEMINI_CLI_HOME'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('GEMINI_CLI_HOME', 'Process')
$previous['GEMINI_API_KEY'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('GEMINI_API_KEY', 'Process')
$previous['GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL'] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL', 'Process')
try {
  $env:GEMINI_CLI_HOME = (Join-Path $HOME '.gemini-tokenlab')
  $env:GEMINI_API_KEY = $env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY
  $env:GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL = 'https://api.tokenlab.sh'
  gemini --model gemini-3.5-flash
} finally {
  foreach ($name in $previous.Keys) {
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable($name, $previous[$name], 'Process')
  }
}
```

These variables apply only to this launch; your saved account, default model and permission settings stay in place. Launch normally without the variables to use your previous setup. Do not persist them in your shell profile.

## Verify

Saving settings or listing models does not verify a key or a completed request. A prompt uses TokenLab balance. Check the reply and its matching [request record](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests) before trying tools; auxiliary requests may also be billed.

```text
Reply only with TOKENLAB_CONNECTION_OK. Do not use tools or modify files.
```

### Pi Coding Agent

> Connect Pi Coding Agent to TokenLab

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/pi-coding-agent

## Let my agent set this up

Copy this task to an agent already running on your computer:

```text
Read this guide and help me connect Pi to TokenLab:
https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/pi-coding-agent
Check my installed version and active configuration first.
Preserve existing accounts, providers, permissions and other settings.
Back up local files and show proposed changes.
Have me enter any API key locally; never ask for, print or paste it in chat.
Check configuration loading first.
Explain any paid request test separately before running it.
```

## Install and configure Pi

Use the current [Pi installation instructions](https://pi.dev/). The npm package is `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`. On Windows, follow the [shell setup](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/windows.md); the CLI uses Git Bash by default. Skip installation when Pi is already available.

```bash
npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.85.1
pi --version
```

The configuration below was checked with **Pi 0.85.1**. Other versions need their own verification against the official documentation.

Back up `~/.pi/agent/models.json`, then append the `tokenlab` entry after existing entries inside `providers`; create the file only if it is absent. A nonempty `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` selects the directory containing `models.json`. Keep existing provider order, `settings.json`, accounts, default-model fields and permissions unchanged. If `tokenlab` already exists in the configuration or saved accounts, use another provider name and update the launch command. Set `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` in the launch environment using [Quickstart](/quickstart) for macOS, Linux, WSL or Windows PowerShell; never put the key in chat.

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "tokenlab": {
      "baseUrl": "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "apiKey": "$TOKENLAB_API_KEY",
      "models": [{ "id": "gpt-5.6-luna" }]
    }
  }
}
```

The leading `$` in `"$TOKENLAB_API_KEY"` is required: a bare `"TOKENLAB_API_KEY"` is a literal string. Choose a current model with Chat Completions and tool support. Set context, output, image and reasoning options from that model’s details instead of copying another model’s limits.

Optional: the [reversible Pi setup helper](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-skills/blob/247bb17c53754c8288d2d5cb00824fbd9f32899b/skills/tokenlab-api-integration/references/pi_setup.md) provides preview, apply and original-file restoration with Python 3.11+. TokenLab Skills plugin **0.1.2** includes these scripts; a standalone Skill installation can also be used after updating to a version that contains them. For an existing plugin or standalone Skill installation, follow the [README update instructions](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-skills/blob/247bb17c53754c8288d2d5cb00824fbd9f32899b/README.md#update-an-existing-installation) and confirm the script is present. The manual configuration here remains usable without the helper.

## Check and restore

Use the same terminal and agent directory to check loading, then select TokenLab explicitly for this session. An unset `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` can hide the provider from the model list. Discovery proves registration and credential presence, not key validity or a completed API request.

```bash
pi --list-models tokenlab
pi --provider tokenlab --model gpt-5.6-luna
```

A prompt uses TokenLab balance. Check the reply and its [request record](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests) before testing tools. To undo the manual configuration, remove only the provider entry you added, preserving all other settings and accounts.

## Skills and MCP

Pi loads [Skills natively](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md). Install the [TokenLab Skill](/integrations/coding-agent-skill) for API integration guidance. MCP requires a separate Pi extension; do not paste an MCP client configuration into `models.json`.

### OpenCode

> Configure OpenCode to use TokenLab API

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/opencode

## Let my agent set this up

Copy this task to an agent already running on your computer:

```text
Read this guide and help me connect OpenCode to TokenLab:
https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/opencode
Check my installed version and active configuration first.
Preserve existing accounts, providers, permissions and other settings.
Back up local files and show proposed changes.
Have me enter any API key locally; never ask for, print or paste it in chat.
Check configuration loading first.
Explain any paid request test separately before running it.
```

## Overview

OpenCode can use TokenLab through a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. Add the TokenLab API key, Base URL, and a current model ID.

## Installation

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/docs/)

```bash
npm install -g opencode-ai@1.18.31
```

Verify installation:

```bash
opencode --version
```

## Configuration

### Step 1: Set Environment Variables

Use the [Quickstart](/quickstart) terminal instructions for macOS, Linux, WSL, or Windows PowerShell to set `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` without putting the key in command history. Launch OpenCode from that terminal. For persistent use, use your local secret manager; do not append a plaintext key to your shell profile.

### Step 2: Configure OpenCode

The configuration below was checked with **OpenCode 1.18.31**. Other versions need their own verification against the official documentation.

Create a separate `~/.config/opencode/tokenlab.jsonc` file with the configuration below. If `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, use `opencode/tokenlab.jsonc` under that directory. Keep the normal `opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc`, accounts, default model and permissions unchanged: this separate file is loaded only for an invocation that selects it with `OPENCODE_CONFIG`. If the file or provider name already belongs to another setup, choose a different file/name and adjust the commands.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "tokenlab": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "TokenLab",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1",
        "apiKey": "{env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY}"
      },
      "models": {
        "gpt-5.6-terra": {
          "name": "GPT-5.6 Terra"
        },
        "gpt-5.6-luna": {
          "name": "GPT-5.6 Luna"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> Note: This configuration uses `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` for Chat Completions. Choose a current model whose details support Chat Completions and the tools you need; do not infer support for another protocol or version from this example.

Optional: the [reversible OpenCode setup helper](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-skills/blob/247bb17c53754c8288d2d5cb00824fbd9f32899b/skills/tokenlab-api-integration/references/opencode_setup.md) provides preview, apply and original-file restoration with Python 3.11+. TokenLab Skills plugin **0.1.2** includes these scripts; a standalone Skill installation can also be used after updating to a version that contains them. For an existing plugin or standalone Skill installation, follow the [README update instructions](https://github.com/hedging8563/tokenlab-skills/blob/247bb17c53754c8288d2d5cb00824fbd9f32899b/README.md#update-an-existing-installation) and confirm the script is present. The manual configuration here remains usable without the helper.

## Basic Usage

Set the key using Quickstart, then load this file and select the model explicitly for this invocation. Substitute your actual path and provider name if customized. Keep any existing `OPENCODE_CONFIG` or inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` setup in a separate launch environment; project and managed settings may still take precedence.

#### macOS / Linux / WSL

```bash macOS / Linux / WSL
OPENCODE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/tokenlab.jsonc" opencode models tokenlab
OPENCODE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/tokenlab.jsonc" opencode --model tokenlab/gpt-5.6-terra
```

#### Windows PowerShell

```powershell Windows PowerShell
$tokenlabConfigRoot = if ($env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME) { $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME } else { Join-Path $HOME '.config' }
$previousConfig = $env:OPENCODE_CONFIG
try {
  $env:OPENCODE_CONFIG = Join-Path $tokenlabConfigRoot 'opencode/tokenlab.jsonc'
  opencode models tokenlab
  opencode --model tokenlab/gpt-5.6-terra
} finally {
  if ($null -eq $previousConfig) {
    Remove-Item Env:OPENCODE_CONFIG -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  } else {
    $env:OPENCODE_CONFIG = $previousConfig
  }
}
```

Model discovery checks local loading, not key validity or a successful live request. A prompt uses TokenLab balance and OpenCode may send separately billed auxiliary requests, such as title generation. Check the reply and the matching [request records](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests).

To use your ordinary setup, launch without this layer. Do not persist `OPENCODE_CONFIG` in your shell profile for this guide. To undo the manual setup, remove only the separate file you created, or restore its backup if it existed before.

## Choose a Model

Copy a current coding model ID from the [Models page](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models). Compare models on your own repository before setting a default.

## Common Commands

**Analyze code:**

```bash
OPENCODE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/tokenlab.jsonc" opencode run --model tokenlab/gpt-5.6-terra "What does this function do?" < src/utils.ts
```

**Generate code:**

```bash
OPENCODE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/tokenlab.jsonc" opencode run --model tokenlab/gpt-5.6-terra "Create a REST API with Express"
```

**Review changes:**

```bash
git diff | OPENCODE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/tokenlab.jsonc" opencode run --model tokenlab/gpt-5.6-terra "Review these changes"
```

**Fix errors:**

```bash
OPENCODE_CONFIG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/tokenlab.jsonc" opencode run --model tokenlab/gpt-5.6-terra "Fix the TypeScript errors in this project"
```

## Interactive Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/help` | Show available commands |
| `/models` | Switch to a different model |
| `/clear` | Clear conversation history |
| `/exit` | Exit OpenCode |

## Troubleshooting

#### Connection Error

- Verify `options.baseURL` is set to `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1`
- Check network connectivity
- Try `curl https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/models` to test

#### Authentication Failed

- Verify `TOKENLAB_API_KEY` environment variable is set
- Verify `options.apiKey` references `{env:TOKENLAB_API_KEY}` or another valid secret source
- Check that the key starts with `sk-`
- Ensure the key is active in TokenLab dashboard

#### Model Not Found

- Check model name in config matches exactly
- Verify model availability at [tokenlab.sh/en/models](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models)

## Tips

#### Use project context

Run OpenCode from your project root for better understanding of your codebase.

#### Choose a model with your own tasks

Test the same edit or review task across a few current models and compare the result, time, and cost.

#### Review generated code

Always review AI-generated code before applying changes to your project.

### OpenHands

> Connect OpenHands to TokenLab

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/openhands

## Overview

Use this page for the OpenHands UI with LiteLLM-backed **Settings → LLM → Advanced** options. Select **OpenAI** and enter a custom model with the `openai/` prefix, a TokenLab key in the local API-key field, and the Base URL below. Record the previous selection first and restore it when finished. Keep existing accounts and tool permissions. See the [official OpenAI-compatible configuration](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/llms/openai-llms). CLI, cloud and source-checkout installations can use different setup flows; follow the instructions for your installed edition. `make setup-config` is not a general installed-CLI command.

## Model Settings

Save the current provider, model and connection settings locally before editing. These controls change the active model selection; restore your previous values when finished. Keep signed-in accounts and tool permissions unchanged. Do not overwrite another OpenAI-compatible connection without a restorable backup.

```text
Custom Model: openai/kimi-k3
Base URL: https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1
```

Saving settings or listing models does not verify a key or a completed request. A prompt uses TokenLab balance. Check the reply and its matching [request record](https://tokenlab.sh/dashboard/runs?section=requests) before trying tools; auxiliary requests may also be billed.

```text
Reply only with TOKENLAB_CONNECTION_OK. Do not use tools or modify files.
```

## Native SDKs

### OpenAI SDK

> Use TokenLab with official OpenAI SDKs and OpenAI-compatible clients

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/openai-sdk

## Overview

Point an OpenAI SDK client to `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1` and use a TokenLab API key. Keep the API method your application already uses, and confirm the selected model supports it through `accepted_request_formats`.

> Note: Python, JavaScript, and Go have official OpenAI SDKs. PHP works well with OpenAI-compatible community clients, but it is not an official OpenAI SDK.

## Installation

#### Python

```bash Python
pip install openai
```

#### JavaScript

```bash JavaScript
npm install openai
```

#### Go

```bash Go
go get github.com/openai/openai-go/v3
```

> Note: Use `POST /v1/responses` for Responses input items, tools, or continuation. Optional fields depend on the selected model.

## Configure the Client

#### Python

```python Python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="sk-your-tokenlab-key",
    base_url="https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1",
)
```

#### JavaScript

```javascript JavaScript
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: 'sk-your-tokenlab-key',
  baseURL: 'https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1',
});
```

#### Go

```go Go
package main

import (
    openai "github.com/openai/openai-go/v3"
    "github.com/openai/openai-go/v3/option"
)

func main() {
    client := openai.NewClient(
        option.WithAPIKey("sk-your-tokenlab-key"),
        option.WithBaseURL("https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1"),
    )

    _ = client
}
```

## Recommended: Chat Completions

#### Python

```python Python
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-5.6-terra",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with: Connected to TokenLab."}]
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

#### JavaScript

```javascript JavaScript
const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'gpt-5.6-terra',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Reply with: Connected to TokenLab.' }],
});

console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
```

#### cURL

```bash cURL
curl https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-tokenlab-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-5.6-terra",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with: Connected to TokenLab."}
    ]
  }'
```

## Advanced: Responses API

Use this path only when your tool or workflow explicitly depends on OpenAI Responses semantics.

### Streaming with Responses

#### Python

```python Python
stream = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5.6-terra",
    input="Write a short poem about coding.",
    stream=True,
)

for event in stream:
    if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
        print(event.delta, end="")
```

#### JavaScript

```javascript JavaScript
const stream = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'gpt-5.6-terra',
  input: 'Write a short poem about coding.',
  stream: true,
});

for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') {
    process.stdout.write(event.delta);
  }
}
```

## Tools / Function Calling

```python
response = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5.6-terra",
    input="What's the weather in Tokyo?",
    tools=[{
        "type": "function",
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get weather for a location",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "location": {"type": "string"}
            },
            "required": ["location"]
        }
    }]
)

for item in response.output:
    if item.type == "function_call":
        print(item.name)
        print(item.arguments)
```

## Vision with Responses

```python
response = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5.6-terra",
    input=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "input_text", "text": "What's in this image?"},
            {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "https://example.com/image.jpg"}
        ]
    }]
)

print(response.output_text)
```

## Embeddings

```python
response = client.embeddings.create(
    model="text-embedding-3-small",
    input="Hello world"
)

print(response.data[0].embedding[:5])
```

## Chat Completions

Chat Completions is the default OpenAI-compatible path for TokenLab:

```python
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-5.6-terra",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}
    ]
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Troubleshooting

#### Connection Error

- Verify the base URL is exactly `https://api.tokenlab.sh/v1`
- Check for proxy interference or custom HTTP client overrides
- Confirm your SDK version supports the method and fields you are using

#### Authentication Failed

- Check that your API key starts with `sk-`
- Verify the key is active in TokenLab dashboard
- Confirm the SDK is sending `Authorization: Bearer ...`

#### Wrong API Path

- `responses.create(...)` sends requests to `/v1/responses`
- `chat.completions.create(...)` sends requests to `/v1/chat/completions`
- Use Chat Completions by default unless you explicitly need Responses-specific behavior

### Anthropic SDK

> Use Claude Messages through TokenLab with the Anthropic SDK

URL: https://docs.tokenlab.sh/integrations/anthropic-sdk

## Overview

The Anthropic SDK can call Claude models through TokenLab's **Messages API**. Change the API key and base URL; the SDK methods stay the same.

> Note: For the Anthropic SDK, use `https://api.tokenlab.sh` as the base URL, without appending `/v1` yourself.

## Installation

#### Python

```bash Python
pip install anthropic
```

#### JavaScript

```bash JavaScript
npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk
```

## Configure the Client

#### Python

```python Python
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    api_key="sk-your-tokenlab-key",
    base_url="https://api.tokenlab.sh",
)
```

#### JavaScript

```javascript JavaScript
import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: 'sk-your-tokenlab-key',
  baseURL: 'https://api.tokenlab.sh',
});
```

## Basic Usage

```python
message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with: Connected to TokenLab."}
    ]
)

print(message.content[0].text)
```

## Streaming

```python
with client.messages.stream(
    model="claude-sonnet-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a short poem about coding."}]
) as stream:
    for text in stream.text_stream:
        print(text, end="", flush=True)
```

## Vision

```python
import base64

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "What's in this image?"},
            {
                "type": "image",
                "source": {
                    "type": "url",
                    "url": "https://example.com/image.jpg"
                }
            }
        ]
    }]
)

with open("image.png", "rb") as f:
    image_data = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image"},
            {
                "type": "image",
                "source": {
                    "type": "base64",
                    "media_type": "image/png",
                    "data": image_data
                }
            }
        ]
    }]
)
```

## Tool Use

```python
message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    tools=[{
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the weather for a location",
        "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "location": {"type": "string"}
            },
            "required": ["location"]
        }
    }],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Tokyo?"}]
)

for block in message.content:
    if block.type == "tool_use":
        print(block.name)
        print(block.input)
```

## Extended Thinking

```python
message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    thinking={
        "type": "enabled",
        "budget_tokens": 10000
    },
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Solve this complex problem step by step."}]
)

for block in message.content:
    if block.type == "thinking":
        print(block.thinking)
    elif block.type == "text":
        print(block.text)
```

## Choose a Model

Copy a current Claude model ID from the [Models page](https://tokenlab.sh/en/models). Compare models on your own prompts before setting a default.

## Troubleshooting

#### Wrong Base URL

- Use `https://api.tokenlab.sh`
- Do not manually append `/v1` when configuring the Anthropic SDK

#### Authentication Failed

- Check that your TokenLab API key starts with `sk-`
- Confirm the key is active in TokenLab dashboard
- Let the Anthropic SDK manage the auth header instead of adding custom headers manually

#### Model Not Found

- Verify the Claude model name exactly
- Check current availability in the TokenLab model catalog
